questions.stem: In a resonance tube experiment, a tube of fixed length closed at one end and several tuning forks of increasing frequency are used to obtain resonance at the open end. If the tuning fork with the lowest frequency which gave resonance had a frequency f1 and the next tuning fork to give resonance had a frequency f2, find the ratio f2/f1.
questions.explanation: A closed tube resonates only at odd harmonics f, 3f, 5f..., so the next resonance after the fundamental is 3f1 and f2/f1 = 3.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Altitude is a height (magnitude only), so it is a scalar; the others have direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about friction is NOT correct?
options: The force of kinetic friction is less than the force of static friction.
The force of kinetic friction between two surfaces is independent of the areas in contact provided the normal reaction is unchanged.
The force of rolling friction between two surfaces is less than the force of sliding friction.
The angle of friction is the angle between the normal reaction and the force of friction.
Friction may be reduced by lubrication.
questions.explanation: The angle of friction is the angle between the normal reaction and the resultant reaction, not the friction force (which is perpendicular to the normal reaction).

questions.stem: The force with which an object is attracted to the earth is called its
questions.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force of the earth on a body (W = mg).

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The refractive index of a liquid is 1.5. If the velocity of light in vacuum is 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, the velocity of light in the liquid is
questions.explanation: v = c/n = 3.0 x 10^8 / 1.5 = 2.0 x 10^8 m/s. (The source misprints the option powers as 10^3.)

questions.stem: If the relative density of a metal is 19, what will be the mass of 20 cm^3 of the metal when immersed in water?
questions.explanation: True mass = 19 x 20 = 380 g; it displaces 20 g of water, so its apparent mass in water is 380 - 20 = 360 g.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about liquid pressure is NOT correct? The pressure
options: at a point in a liquid is proportional to the depth.
at any point in a liquid is the same at the same level.
is exerted equally in all directions at any point.
of a liquid at any point on the wall of its container acts in a direction perpendicular to the wall.
at a particular depth depends on the shape of the vessel.
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure p = h(rho)g depends only on depth and density, not on the shape of the vessel.

questions.stem: A ship travelling towards a cliff receives the echo of its whistle after 3.5 seconds. A short while later, it receives the echo after 2.5 seconds. If the speed of sound in air under the prevailing conditions is 250 m/s, how much closer is the ship to the cliff?
questions.explanation: Distances are vt/2: 250 x 3.5/2 = 437.5 m and 250 x 2.5/2 = 312.5 m; the difference is 125 m.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about defects of vision is/are CORRECT?
I. For a long sighted person, close objects appear blurred.
II. For a short sighted person, distant objects appear blurred.
III. Short sight is corrected by using a pair of converging lenses.
questions.explanation: I and II are true; short sight is corrected with diverging (concave) lenses, so III is false.

questions.stem: The range of wavelengths of the visible spectrum is 400 nm - 700 nm. The wavelength of gamma rays is
options: shorter than 700 nm but longer than 400 nm
questions.explanation: Gamma rays lie beyond ultraviolet at the short-wavelength end of the spectrum, so their wavelength is shorter than 400 nm.

questions.stem: A train has an initial velocity of 44 m/s and an acceleration of -4 m/s^2. Its velocity after 10 seconds is

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem:
Which of the following conditions are necessary and sufficient for total internal reflection to take place at the boundary between two optical media?
I. Light is passing from optically denser medium to optically less dense medium.
II. Light is passing from optically less dense medium to optically denser medium.
III. Angle of incidence is greater (than the critical angle).
IV. Angle of incidence is lesser (than the critical angle).
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs light going from the denser to the less dense medium with angle of incidence greater than the critical angle.

questions.stem: A man of mass 50 kg ascends a flight of stairs 5 m high in 5 seconds. If acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/s^2, the power expended is
Which of the following arrangements in the sequence shown can be used to obtain a pure spectrum of white light?
options: Source, slit, converging lens, prism, converging lens, screen.
Source, converging lens, prism, diverging lens, screen.
Source, slit, prism, diverging lens, screen.
questions.explanation: A pure spectrum needs a narrow slit, a converging lens to give a parallel beam into the prism, and a second converging lens to focus each colour on the screen.

questions.stem:
It is usual to transmit electric power at high voltage and low current. Which of the following are possible advantages of the method?
I. Heat losses are reduced because the currents are small.
II. Thin wires can be used because small currents are flowing.
III. The power can flow faster because the voltage is high.
questions.explanation: Small currents reduce I^2R losses and allow thinner cables; voltage does not make power 'flow faster'.

questions.stem: A 24 V potential difference is applied across a parallel combination of four 6-ohm resistors. The current in each resistor is
questions.explanation: Each resistor has the full 24 V across it: I = 24/6 = 4 A.

questions.stem: The electrochemical equivalent of a metal is 0.126 x 10^-6 kg/C. The mass of the metal that a current of 5 A deposits from a suitable bath in 1 hour is
Ripples on water are similar to light waves in that they both
questions.explanation: Both are transverse waves that show reflection, refraction and diffraction.

questions.stem: A piece of wood is floating on water. The forces acting on the wood are
questions.explanation: A floating body is in equilibrium under its weight and the upthrust of the water.

questions.stem: A force of 16 N is applied to a 4.0 kg block that is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. What is the velocity of the block at t = 5 seconds?

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
I. The mass number is equal to the total number of protons and electrons in an atom.
II. The atomic number is equal to the number of protons in an atom.
III. The number of electrons in an atom is equal to the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
questions.explanation: Atomic number = number of protons; mass number = protons + neutrons, so only II is correct.

questions.stem: A short response time is obtained in a liquid-in-glass thermometer when the
options: bulb is high density and the bore is large.
bulb is thin-walled and the liquid is a good conductor of heat.
questions.explanation: A thin-walled bulb and a liquid that conducts heat well let the liquid reach the surrounding temperature quickly.

questions.stem: A machine has a velocity ratio of 5. It requires a 50 kg weight to overcome a 200 kg weight. The efficiency is

If the normal atmospheric pressure in a laboratory supports a column of mercury 0.76 m high and the relative density of mercury is 13.8, then the height of water column which atmospheric pressure will support in the same laboratory at the same time is
questions.explanation: h(water) = 0.76 x 13.8 = 10.5 m, i.e. about 10 m.

questions.stem: An electric current of 3 A flowing through an electric heating element of resistance 20 ohms embedded in 1,000 g of an oil raises the temperature of the oil by 10 °C in 10 seconds, then the specific heat capacity of the oil is

The difference of potential between the terminals of a cell is 2.2 volts. When a 4 ohm resistor is connected across the terminals of this cell, the potential difference is 2 volts. What is the internal resistance of the cell?

QR is a vertical conductor (Q above R) and the current I flows from R to Q. P is a point on the horizontal plane and it is to the South of the wire. The direction of the magnetic field at P due to the current is
questions.explanation: The current flows upward; by the right-hand grip rule the field circles anticlockwise seen from above, which points East at a point south of the wire.

questions.stem:
Which of the following may be used to determine relative humidity in a physics laboratory?
I. Manometer
II. Wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer
III. Hair hygrometer
IV. A hydrometer
questions.explanation: Wet-and-dry bulb and hair hygrometers measure humidity; a manometer measures pressure and a hydrometer measures relative density.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: PQ is a thin rod on a horizontal table, RS is a plane mirror inclined at 45° to the horizontal. The image of PQ as seen in the mirror by the eye, T, is
questions.explanation: A plane mirror at 45° to the horizontal turns the image of a horizontal object through 90°, so the image is vertical.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The speed of light in vacuum is 3.0 x 10^8 m/s. If the refractive index of a transparent liquid is 4/3 then the speed of light in the liquid is
If the force on a charge of 0.2 coulomb in an electric field is 4 N, then the electric field intensity of the field is
The specific latent heat of vaporization of a substance is always
options: less than its specific latent heat of fusion.
greater than its specific latent heat of fusion.
equal to its specific latent heat of fusion.
all of the above depending on the nature of the substance
questions.explanation: Separating molecules completely (vaporization) needs much more energy per kg than loosening them (fusion).

questions.stem: Longitudinal waves do not exhibit
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarized.

questions.stem: The distance travelled by a particle starting from rest is plotted against the square of the time elapsed from the commencement of motion. The resulting graph is linear. The slope of this graph is a measure of
questions.explanation: From rest, s = (1/2)at^2, so a graph of s against t^2 has slope a/2.

questions.stem: PT is a uniform metre rule pivoted at R, the 70 cm mark. Two forces 0.1 N and 0.4 N are applied (vertically downwards) at Q, the 60 cm mark, and S, the 85 cm mark. If the metre rule is kept in equilibrium by the forces and its weight, then the weight of the metre rule is
questions.explanation: Moments about R (weight acts at 50 cm): W x 20 + 0.1 x 10 = 0.4 x 15, so W = 5/20 = 0.25 N.

questions.stem:
For which of the underlisted quantities is the derived unit ML^2T^-2 correct?
I. Moment of a force
II. Work
III. Acceleration
questions.explanation: Moment (N m) and work (J = N m) both have dimensions ML^2T^-2; acceleration is LT^-2.

questions.stem: What volume of alcohol with a density of 8.4 x 10^2 kg/m^3 will have the same mass as 4.2 m^3 of petrol whose density is 7.2 x 10^2 kg/m^3?
questions.explanation: Mass of petrol = 4.2 x 720 = 3024 kg; volume of alcohol = 3024/840 = 3.6 m^3.

questions.stem: For correcting long sight defects in the human eye we require a
questions.explanation: Long sight (hypermetropia) is corrected with a converging (convex) lens.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: For a concave mirror to form a real diminished image, the object must be placed
options: between the mirror and the focus
between the focus and the centre of curvature
at a distance greater than the radius of curvature
questions.explanation: A concave mirror gives a real, diminished image only when the object is beyond the centre of curvature.

questions.stem: The unit quantity of electricity is called
questions.explanation: Quantity of electricity (charge) is measured in coulombs.

questions.stem: The resistance of a wire depends on
questions.explanation: R = (rho)L/A, and resistivity varies with temperature, so all the factors apply.

questions.stem: Two cells, each of e.m.f. 1.5 V and an internal resistance 2 ohms, are connected in parallel. Calculate the current flowing when the cells are connected to a 1 ohm resistor.
questions.explanation: In parallel the e.m.f. stays 1.5 V and the internal resistance is 1 ohm, so I = 1.5/(1 + 1) = 0.75 A. (The source prints the options in ohms by mistake.)

questions.stem: Which of the following components is NOT contained in a dry cell?
questions.explanation: A Leclanche dry cell has a zinc case, a carbon rod, manganese(IV) oxide and ammonium chloride paste; there is no copper rod.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be described as high tension transmission?
questions.explanation: High-tension transmission sends power at high voltage and low current to cut I^2R losses.

questions.stem: All the heat generated in a 5 ohm resistor by 2 A flowing for 30 seconds is used to evaporate 5 g of liquid at its boiling point. Which of the following is the correct value of the specific latent heat of the liquid?
When vibration occurs in an air column, the distance between a node and an antinode is equal to
questions.explanation: Adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart, so a node and the next antinode are a quarter wavelength apart.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements is (are) NOT correct?
I. Pressure changes do not affect the speed of sound in air.
II. The velocity of sound increases with temperature.
III. The quality of a note depends only on its frequency.
questions.explanation: Quality (timbre) depends on the overtones present, not only on frequency; I and II are true.

questions.stem: Of two identical tuning forks with natural frequency 256 Hz, one is loaded so that 4 beats per second are heard when they are sounded together. What is the frequency of the loaded tuning fork?
questions.explanation: Loading a fork lowers its frequency, so it is 256 - 4 = 252 Hz.

questions.stem: Dew point is the temperature at which water vapour in the atmosphere
options: Is just sufficient to cause cooling
Has a relative humidity of fifty percent
questions.explanation: At the dew point the air is just saturated and the vapour begins to condense.

questions.stem: The lower and upper fixed points marked on a mercury-in-glass thermometer are 210 mm apart. The end of the mercury column in the tube is 49 mm above the lower fixed point in a room. What is the temperature of the room in degrees Celsius?
If a solid changes directly into a gas when heat is applied the process is called
questions.explanation: A direct solid-to-gas change is sublimation.

questions.stem: A plane inclined at an angle of 30° to the horizontal has an efficiency of 60%. The force parallel to the plane required to push a load of 120 N uniformly up the plane is

A body of mass 5 kg initially at rest is acted upon by two mutually perpendicular forces 12 N and 5 N. If the particle moves in the direction of the resultant force, calculate the magnitude of the acceleration.

Which of the following statements describes an atom accurately?
I. Atoms of all elements are identical.
II. An atom contains a nucleus and a number of electrons.
III. Due to the electrons in the atom, an atom is negatively charged.
IV. Electrons in the atom move in circular orbits round the nucleus.
questions.explanation: In the (Bohr) model an atom has a nucleus with electrons in circular orbits; atoms are neutral and differ between elements.

questions.stem: A particle moves in a circular orbit of radius 0.02 m. If the speed of the particle is 0.88 m/s, calculate its frequency in cycles per second.
Heat is supplied uniformly at the rate of 100 W to 1.0 x 10^-2 kg of a liquid for 20 seconds. If the temperature of the liquid rises by 5 °C, then the specific heat capacity of the liquid is

A given mass of an ideal gas occupies a volume V at a temperature T and under a pressure P. If the pressure is increased to 2P and the temperature reduced to T/2, then the percentage change in the volume of the gas is
questions.explanation: V2 = V x (P/2P) x ((T/2)/T) = V/4, a 75% decrease.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties of matter CANNOT be utilized for temperature measurement? The
options: Volume of a gas at constant pressure
Pressure of a gas at constant volume
Current produced in a photoelectric effect
questions.explanation: Photoelectric current depends on the light falling on the surface, not on temperature; the others are standard thermometric properties.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about the compound microscope and astronomical telescope is (are) correct?
I. The final image of a compound microscope is located at infinity.
II. The final image of the astronomical telescope is always erect.
III. The objective lens of a compound microscope has a very short focal length.
questions.explanation: A microscope's objective has a very short focal length; its final image is normally at the near point, and the astronomical telescope gives an inverted image.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A coin is placed at the bottom of a cube of glass t cm thick. If the refractive index of the glass is n, how high does the coin appear to be raised to an observer looking perpendicularly into the glass?
questions.explanation: Apparent depth = t/n, so the displacement is t - t/n = t(n - 1)/n.

questions.stem: A gun of mass 2.0 kg fires a bullet of mass 1.6 x 10^-2 kg due East. If the bullet leaves the nozzle of the gun with a velocity of 150 m/s, what is the recoil velocity of the gun?
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: v = (0.016 x 150)/2.0 = 1.2 m/s, opposite to the bullet (West).

questions.stem: Normal atmospheric pressure at sea-level is 10^5 N/m^2 and the acceleration due to gravity is approximately 10 m/s^2. If the atmosphere has a uniform density of 1 kg/m^3, its height is
Which of the following is a correct explanation of the inertia of a body?
options: Ability to overcome the earth's gravity
Reluctance to start moving and its readiness to stop moving once it has begun to move
Reluctance to start moving and its reluctance to stop moving once it has begun to move
questions.explanation: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion.

questions.stem: If a water pump at Kainji Dam is capable of lifting 1000 kg of water through a vertical height of 10 m in 10 s, the power of the pump is (g = 10 m/s^2)
What is the apparent colour of a RED SHIRT when viewed in PURE green light?
questions.explanation: A red shirt absorbs green light and there is no red light to reflect, so it looks black.

questions.stem: The spectrum of white light consists of coloured lights arranged in the following order
options: Blue, red, green, yellow, indigo, violet, orange.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.
Red, orange, yellow, indigo, green, blue, violet.
Indigo, green, blue, violet, yellow, red, orange.
Yellow, blue, green, violet, orange, indigo, red.
questions.explanation: The order is ROYGBIV: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.stem: Cathode rays are
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of fast-moving electrons.

questions.stem: A device that converts sound energy into electrical energy is
options: The horn of a motor car
questions.explanation: A microphone converts sound into electrical signals; a loudspeaker does the reverse.

questions.stem:
Which of the following
I. beta-particles
II. Protons
III. Neutrons
IV. alpha-particles
may be found in light nuclei?
questions.explanation: Nuclei are made up of protons and neutrons only.

questions.stem: Radio waves have a velocity of 3 x 10^8 m/s. A radio station sends out a broadcast on a frequency of 800 kHz. The wavelength of the broadcast is
What is the cost of running five 50 W lamps and four 100 W lamps for 10 hours if electrical energy costs 2 kobo per kWh?
questions.explanation: Energy = (250 + 400) W x 10 h = 6.5 kWh; cost = 6.5 x 2 = 13 kobo = N0.13.

questions.stem: A galvanometer of resistance 5.0 ohms has full-scale deflection for a current of 100 mA. How would its range be extended to 1.0 A? By placing a resistance of
questions.explanation: Shunt current = 1.0 - 0.1 = 0.9 A; R = (0.1 x 5)/0.9 = 5/9 ohm, connected in parallel.

questions.stem: An insulated cylindrical coil of copper wire is wound round a paper tube. The ends of the coil are connected to a sensitive galvanometer. When a magnet was plunged into the coil it was observed that the galvanometer needle gave a deflection. Which of the following correctly describes this experiment?
options: The effect illustrated is induced electromotive force.
The strength of the current produced is inversely proportional to the speed with which the magnet is plunged into the coil.
The direction of the current is always such as to enhance the change producing it.
The galvanometer gave a permanent deflection.
On removing the magnet from the coil the galvanometer deflected in the same direction.
questions.explanation: Moving the magnet changes the flux linkage and induces an e.m.f. (Faraday); the deflection is momentary and reverses when the magnet is withdrawn.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental S.I. unit?
questions.explanation: The radian is a supplementary (dimensionless) unit; metre, ampere, kelvin and second are base SI units.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum with a period of 2.0 s has its length doubled. Its new period is
questions.explanation: T is proportional to sqrt(L), so the new period is 2.0 x sqrt(2) = 2.83 s.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about the spring balance and the chemical balance?
I. Both are used to measure the mass of an object.
II. Either of them may be used to measure the weight of an object.
III. The spring balance works on the principle of Hooke's law while the chemical balance works on the principle of moments.
IV. A change in gravity changes the readings of a spring balance but not that of a chemical balance.
questions.explanation: A spring balance measures weight (Hooke's law) and its reading changes with g; a chemical balance compares masses by moments, so its reading does not.

questions.stem:
Which of the following types of motion are oscillatory?
I. A diving board when used by a diver.
II. The motion of the balance wheel of a wrist watch.
III. The motion of the turn-table of a record player.
IV. The motion of the centre of a ten kobo piece as it rolls down an inclined plane.
V. The motion of the needle of a D.C. ammeter into which a low A.C. current is passed.
questions.explanation: The diving board, the balance wheel and the needle driven by a.c. move to and fro; a turntable rotates and the coin's centre moves in a line.

questions.stem: If a car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 10 m/s^2 for ten seconds, the distance it covers in the last one second of the motion is

A block of mass 2.0 kg resting on a smooth horizontal plane is acted upon simultaneously by two forces, 10 N due North and 10 N due East. The magnitude of the acceleration produced by the forces on the block is

A metal block of mass 5 kg lies on a rough horizontal platform. If a horizontal force of 8 N applied to the block through its centre of mass just slides the block on the platform, then the coefficient of limiting friction between the block and the platform is (take g = 10 m/s^2)
Which of the following is NOT a force?
questions.explanation: Impulse is force x time (a change in momentum), not a force.

questions.stem: Two masses 40 g and 60 g respectively, are attached firmly to the ends of a light metre rule. The centre of gravity of the system is
options: At the mid-point of the metre rule
indeterminate because the metre-rule is light
questions.explanation: Taking moments from the lighter mass: x = (60 x 100)/100 = 60 cm, i.e. 40 cm from the heavier mass.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A force of 100 N stretches an elastic string to a total length of 20 cm. If an additional force of 100 N stretches the string 5 cm further, find the natural length of the string.
questions.explanation: 100 N produces 5 cm extension, so the natural length is 20 - 5 = 15 cm.

questions.stem: Two divers G and H are at depths 20 m and 40 m respectively below the water surface in a lake. The pressure on G is P1 while the pressure on H is P2. If the atmospheric pressure is equivalent to 10 m of water, then the value of P2/P1 is
The areas of the effort and load pistons of a hydraulic press are 0.5 m^2 and 5 m^2 respectively. If a force F1 of 100 N is applied on the effort piston, the force F2 on the load is
questions.explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally: F2 = 100 x 5/0.5 = 1000 N.

questions.stem: A metal cube of volume 10^3 mm^3 is lowered into a measuring cylinder containing water. If the internal cross-sectional area of the cylinder is 1.5 x 10^2 mm^2, by how much does the water level rise in the cylinder?
questions.explanation: Rise = volume/area = 1000/150 = 6.67 mm.

questions.stem: A uniform cylindrical block of wood floats in water with one-third of its height above the water level. In a liquid of relative density 0.8, what fraction of its height will be above the liquid level?
questions.explanation: Relative density of wood = 2/3; in the liquid the immersed fraction = (2/3)/0.8 = 5/6, so 1/6 is above.

questions.stem: A thin aluminium plate has a surface area of 1.500 m^2 at 20 °C. What will be its surface area when it is cooled to -20 °C? (Take the linear expansivity of aluminium to be 2.5 x 10^-5 K^-1)

Two liquids, P at a temperature of 20 °C and Q at a temperature of 80 °C have specific heat capacities of 1.0 J kg^-1 °C^-1 and 1.5 J kg^-1 °C^-1 respectively. If equal masses of P and Q are mixed in a lagged calorimeter, then the equilibrium temperature is

A quantity of gas occupies a certain volume when the temperature is -73 °C and the pressure is 1.5 atmospheres. If the pressure is increased to 4.5 atmospheres and the volume is halved at the same time, what will be the new temperature of the gas?
In a gas experiment, the pressure of the gas is plotted against the reciprocal of the volume of the gas at a constant temperature. The unit of the slope of the resulting curve is
questions.explanation: Slope = P/(1/V) = PV, whose unit N/m^2 x m^3 = N m, the unit of work.

questions.stem: Water shows anomalous behaviour
questions.explanation: Water contracts on heating from 0 °C to 4 °C instead of expanding; this is its anomalous expansion.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Boiling occurs when the saturated vapour pressure of the liquid involved equals the external pressure.
Both the boiling point and the saturated vapour pressure of a given liquid depend on the external pressure.
The saturated vapour pressure rises with increase in temperature.
The saturated vapour pressure is independent of the volume available for the vapour.
It is possible to boil water at a lower temperature than 100 °C at high altitude.
questions.explanation: Saturated vapour pressure depends only on temperature, not on the external pressure (only the boiling point does).

questions.stem: Which of the following phenomena CANNOT be explained by the molecular theory of matter?
questions.explanation: Radiation is energy carried by electromagnetic waves and needs no particles of matter.

questions.stem: In order to find the depth of the sea, a ship sends out a sound wave and receives an echo after one second. If the velocity of sound in water is 1500 m/s, what is the depth of the sea?
When a sound wave passes from air into water its
options: speed and frequency increase but its wavelength remains the same.
speed and wavelength increase but its frequency remains the same
speed remains the same but its frequency and wavelength change.
speed increases but its frequency and wavelength decrease.
questions.explanation: Frequency is fixed by the source; sound travels faster in water so its wavelength increases too.

questions.stem: If the fundamental frequency of a closed pipe organ on a day when the speed of sound is 340 m/s is 170 Hz, then the length of the pipe is
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe f = v/4L, so L = 340/(4 x 170) = 0.5 m = 50 cm.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An object is placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius 40 cm. The image formed is
options: Virtual and 60 cm behind the mirror
Real and 60 cm in front of the mirror
Virtual and 40 cm from the mirror
questions.explanation: f = 20 cm; 1/v = 1/20 - 1/15 = -1/60, so v = -60 cm: virtual, 60 cm behind the mirror.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A 45° triangular glass prism can be used as a reflector of light because
options: Refraction never takes place in such a prism
The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence
The refractive index of glass is less than 1
The critical angle for glass is less than 45°
questions.explanation: Light meets the hypotenuse face at 45°, which exceeds the critical angle of glass (about 42°), so it is totally internally reflected.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem:
A convex mirror is used as a driving mirror because
I. Its image is erect
II. It has a large field of view
III. It has a long focal length
Identify the CORRECT statement(s).
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always gives an erect, diminished image and a wide field of view.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Two rays of light from a point below the surface of water are equally inclined to the vertical and are inclined to each other at 60° in water. What is the angle between the rays when they emerge into air? (Take the refractive index of water to be 4/3)
questions.explanation: Each ray meets the surface at 30°; sin r = (4/3) sin 30° = 0.667, r = 41.8°, so the angle between them is 83.6°.

questions.stem: A narrow beam of white light can be split up into different colours by a glass prism. The correct explanation is that
options: White light is an electromagnetic wave
The prism has all the colours of the white light
White light has undergone total internal reflection in the prism
Different colours of white light travel with different speeds in glass
White light consists of yellow, green and red colours
questions.explanation: Each colour travels at a different speed in glass, so each is refracted by a different amount (dispersion).

questions.stem: A charge of one coulomb liberates 0.0033 g of copper in an electrolytic process. How long will it take a current of 2 A to liberate 1.98 g of copper in such a process?
questions.explanation: Charge needed = 1.98/0.0033 = 600 C; t = 600/2 = 300 s = 5 minutes.

questions.stem: Which of the following will convert a milliammeter to a voltmeter?
options: Parallel resistance equal to milliammeter resistance
questions.explanation: A high resistance (multiplier) in series converts a milliammeter into a voltmeter.

questions.stem: A wire P has half the diameter and half the length of a wire Q of similar material. The ratio of the resistance of P to that of Q is
questions.explanation: R is proportional to L/d^2: (1/2)/(1/2)^2 = 2, so R_P : R_Q = 2 : 1.

questions.stem: An electric kettle, connected to a 240 V mains, produces 6.0 x 10^5 J of heat energy to boil a quantity of water in 5 minutes. Find the resistance of the kettle.
A current I passes through a parallel combination of a 5 ohm and a 10 ohm resistor. If the power dissipated in the 5 ohm resistor is 40 W, then the power dissipated in the 10 ohm resistor is
questions.explanation: In parallel the voltage is the same, so P is proportional to 1/R: P = 40 x 5/10 = 20 W.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: A galvanometer can be converted to an ammeter with a different range by connecting a high resistance in series.
An electric current always produces a magnetic field.
Maxwell's screw rule states that if a corkscrew moves in the direction of the current, the hand turns in the direction of the lines of force.
Electromagnets are used in electric bells and telephone receivers.
The lines of force round a straight current carrying conductor are circular.
questions.explanation: A galvanometer becomes an ammeter with a low resistance shunt in parallel; a high series resistance makes it a voltmeter.

questions.stem: A transformer has a primary coil with 500 turns and secondary coil with 2500 turns. When the voltage input to the primary coil is 120 V, the output is
Which of the following statements about electrolysis is NOT correct?
options: The substances in solution in the electrolyte become ionized.
Ions are electrically charged and are attracted towards electrodes when a potential difference is applied.
Ions may be discharged at the electrodes, forming bubbles or deposits.
The mass deposited depends upon the length of time for which current flows.
The mass of gas set free or metal deposited is proportional to the square of the current.
questions.explanation: By Faraday's first law the mass liberated is proportional to the quantity of charge It, i.e. to the current, not its square.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: The average range of distinct vision for a normal eye is from the far distance (infinity) up to about 25 cm in front of the eye.
Longsighted people have difficulty in making the eye lens sufficiently powerful to focus on nearby objects.
Shortsighted people cannot accommodate distant objects.
Longsighted people need diverging spectacle lenses.
A person with long sight has his eye-ball too short and the image of an object is therefore formed behind the retina.
questions.explanation: Long sight is corrected with converging (convex) lenses, not diverging ones.

questions.stem: What is the number of neutrons in the uranium isotope with mass number 238 and atomic number 92?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 238 - 92 = 146.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A graph of force against extension is plotted for a spiral spring. The force constant of the spring is given by the
options: Slope of the linear portion of the graph.
Length of the linear portion of the graph.
Area under the linear portion of the graph.
questions.explanation: Within the elastic limit F = ke, so k is the slope of the linear part of the force-extension graph.

questions.stem: A heavy object is suspended from a string and lowered into water so that it is completely submerged. The object appears lighter because
options: The density of water is less than that of the object.
The pressure is low just below the water surface.
The tension in the string neutralizes part of the weight.
questions.explanation: By Archimedes' principle the water exerts an upthrust equal to the weight of water displaced.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a derived unit?
questions.explanation: The newton (kg m s^-2) is derived from base units; the others are base units.

questions.stem: Two objects, one having three times the mass of the other, are dropped at the same time from a tall building. When they are above the ground, the two objects will have the same
questions.explanation: All freely falling bodies have the same acceleration g, regardless of mass.

questions.stem: Which of the following is in a neutral equilibrium?
options: A heavy weight suspended on a string.
A cone resting on its slant edge.
The beam of a balance in use.
questions.explanation: A cone on its slant edge can roll without raising or lowering its centre of gravity, so it is in neutral equilibrium.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically into the air with an initial velocity u. What is the greatest height reached?
questions.explanation: At the top v = 0: 0 = u^2 - 2gH, so H = u^2/2g.

questions.stem: Which of the following assumptions is made in a simple pendulum experiment? The
options: Initial angle of oscillation must be large
questions.explanation: A simple pendulum assumes a light inextensible string, a point bob and small-angle oscillations.

questions.stem: Three forces F1, F2 and F3 acting at O are in equilibrium. F1 and F2 are inclined at 60° to each other. If the magnitude of F1 is 10.0 N and the magnitude of F2 is 5.0 N, find the magnitude of F3.
questions.explanation: F3 balances the resultant of F1 and F2: sqrt(10^2 + 5^2 + 2 x 10 x 5 x cos 60°) = sqrt(175) = 13.2 N.

questions.stem: When a box of mass 400 g is given an initial speed of 5 m/s, it slides along a horizontal floor a distance of 3 m before coming to rest. What is the coefficient of the kinetic friction between the box and the floor? (g = 10 m/s^2)
A constant force of magnitude F acts on an object of mass 0.04 kg initially at rest at a point O. If the speed of the object when it has moved 50 m from O is 500 m/s, what is the value of F?
questions.explanation: Work done = KE gained: F x 50 = (1/2)(0.04)(500^2) = 5000 J, so F = 100 N.

questions.stem: A rectangular tank contains water to a depth of 2 m. If the base is 4 m x 3 m, calculate the force on the base. (Density of water = 10^3 kg/m^3, g = 10 m/s^2)
A 1000 kg elevator is descending vertically with an acceleration of 1.0 m/s^2. If the acceleration due to gravity is 10.0 m/s^2, the tension in the suspending cable is
questions.explanation: mg - T = ma, so T = m(g - a) = 1000 x 9 = 9000 N.

questions.stem: The mode of heat transfer which does not require a material medium is
questions.explanation: Radiation travels as electromagnetic waves and can cross a vacuum.

questions.stem: The expansion of solids can be considered a disadvantage in the
questions.explanation: Expansion of a watch's balance wheel changes its timing; the other examples make use of expansion.

questions.stem: In an experiment in which molten naphthalene is allowed to cool, a cooling curve was obtained. The temperature 80 °C (at which the curve is flat) is known as the
questions.explanation: The flat part of the cooling curve of naphthalene at about 80 °C is where it solidifies, i.e. its melting (freezing) point.

questions.stem: The specific latent heat of fusion of lead is the amount of heat required to
options: Melt lead at its melting point
Heat a unit mass of lead through 1 °C
Change the state of a unit mass of lead at its melting point.
Change the state of a unit mass of lead at its boiling point.
questions.explanation: Specific latent heat of fusion is the heat needed to change unit mass of solid to liquid at its melting point without change in temperature.

questions.stem: Which of the following is common to evaporation and boiling? They
options: Take place at a definite pressure.
questions.explanation: Both turn liquid into vapour; only evaporation occurs at any temperature and only at the surface.

questions.stem: Mercury is suitable as a barometric fluid because it
options: Is several times denser than water
Is a good conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Its high density (13.6 times water) gives a short, convenient column of about 76 cm.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties makes metals ideal for cooking utensils?
questions.explanation: Metals conduct heat well, passing heat quickly from the flame to the food.

questions.stem: A gas occupies a volume of 300 cm^3 at a temperature of 27 °C. What is its volume at 54 °C, when the pressure is constant?
questions.explanation: Charles' law: V2 = 300 x 327/300 = 327 cm^3 (temperatures in kelvin).

questions.stem: When two objects P and Q are supplied with the same quantity of heat, the temperature change in P is observed to be twice that of Q. The mass of P is half that of Q. The ratio of the specific heat capacity of P to Q is
questions.explanation: (m/2)c_P(2dT) = m c_Q dT gives c_P = c_Q, a ratio of 1 : 1.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A ray of light in air strikes a glass plate at an angle of incidence of 60°. The reflected ray is observed to be perpendicular to the refracted ray. What is the refractive index of the glass?
questions.explanation: If reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, r = 90° - 60° = 30°; n = sin 60°/sin 30° = 1.73.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A lens of focal length 12.0 cm forms an upright image three times the size of a real object. The distance between the object and the image is
questions.explanation: Upright magnified image: converging lens with v = -3u; 1/12 = 1/u - 1/3u gives u = 8 cm, v = 24 cm on the same side, so they are 16 cm apart.

questions.stem: In which of the following arrangements is the wavelength in an increasing order?
options: Gamma rays, infra-red rays, X-rays, radiowaves.
Gamma rays, X-rays, infra-red rays, radiowaves.
Radiowaves, X-rays, gamma rays, infra-red rays.
Infra-red rays, radiowaves, X-rays, gamma rays.
questions.explanation: Wavelength increases from gamma rays to X-rays to infra-red to radio waves.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: If the refractive index of glass is 1.5, what is the critical angle at the air-glass interface?

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A dentist obtains a linear magnification of 4 of a hole in a tooth by placing a concave mirror at a distance of 2.0 cm from the tooth. The radius of curvature of the mirror is
questions.explanation: Virtual image: v = -8 cm; 1/f = 1/2 - 1/8 = 3/8, f = 2.67 cm, so r = 2f = 5.3 cm.

questions.stem: What is the effect of the increase in the size of the hole of a pin-hole camera on the image? It
options: Brings the image into sharper focus.
questions.explanation: A larger hole lets many overlapping images form, so the image becomes brighter but blurred.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A pencil is placed vertically between a concave mirror and its focal point. The image of the pencil in the mirror will be
questions.explanation: An object inside the focal length of a concave mirror gives a virtual, erect, magnified image.

questions.stem: A wave of frequency 10 Hz forms a stationary wave pattern in a medium where the velocity is 20 cm/s. The distance between adjacent nodes is
questions.explanation: lambda = v/f = 20/10 = 2 cm; adjacent nodes are lambda/2 = 1.0 cm apart.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the loudness of sound? It
options: Depends on the square of the amplitude of the vibrating body.
Is proportional to the distance of the observer from the source of the sound.
questions.explanation: Loudness depends on intensity, which is proportional to the square of the amplitude.

questions.stem: A man clapping his hands at regular intervals observes that the echo of a clap coincides with the next clap. If the reflecting cliff is 160 m away and the speed of sound is 320 m/s, what is the frequency of the clapping?
questions.explanation: Echo time = 2 x 160/320 = 1 s between claps, so the frequency is 1 Hz.

questions.stem: The vibration of an air column produces the sound in the
questions.explanation: A flute is a wind instrument: its sound comes from a vibrating air column.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a part of a d.c. electric motor?
questions.explanation: A d.c. motor has a field magnet, an armature coil, a commutator and brushes, but no transformer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is stored by a dry Leclanche cell?
questions.explanation: A cell stores chemical energy which it converts to electrical energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of magnetism?
options: Iron filings cling mainly round the ends of a bar magnet.
The freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest in the geographic north-south direction.
questions.explanation: Magnetism is strongest at the poles near the ends, so iron filings cluster there; a suspended magnet rests along the magnetic (not geographic) meridian.

questions.stem: The angle between the magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian at a locality on the earth is the
options: Angle of inclination at the locality
Angle of declination of the locality.
questions.explanation: The angle between the magnetic and geographic meridians is the declination (variation).

questions.stem: The sign of the charge on a charged glass rod may be determined with
questions.explanation: Bringing the rod near an electroscope of known charge: an increase in leaf divergence shows like charge.

questions.stem: The wavelength of ultraviolet radiation is 400 nm. If the speed of light in air is 3 x 10^8 m/s, then the frequency of the ultraviolet radiation is
Which of the following is most strongly deflected by a magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Beta particles are charged and very light, so they are deflected most; gamma and X-rays are uncharged.

questions.stem: Which of the following units is equivalent to kg m s^-1?
questions.explanation: kg m s^-1 = (kg m s^-2) x s = N s, the unit of momentum/impulse.

questions.stem: A man walks 8 km north and then 5 km in a direction 60° east of north. Find the distance from his starting point.
questions.explanation: Angle between the two displacements is 60°, so R = sqrt(8^2 + 5^2 + 2(8)(5)cos 60°) = sqrt(129) = 11.36 km.

questions.stem: A jet engine develops a thrust of 270 N when the velocity of the exhaust gases relative to the engine is 300 m s^-1. What is the mass of the material ejected per second?
questions.explanation: Thrust = (mass ejected per second) x velocity, so m/t = 270/300 = 0.90 kg per second.

questions.stem: An elevator of mass 4800 kg is supported by a cable which can safely withstand a maximum tension of 60 000 N. The maximum upward acceleration the elevator can have is (g = 10 m s^-2)

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A 50.0 kg block is dropped on a spring from a point 10 m above. If the force constant of the spring is 4.0 x 10^4 N m^-1, find the maximum compression of the spring. (g = 10 m s^-2)
questions.explanation: Potential energy lost ≈ elastic energy stored: mgh = ½kx^2, so 5000 = ½(4.0 x 10^4)x^2 and x = 0.50 m.

questions.stem: A constant force of 40 N acting on a body initially at rest gives an acceleration of 0.1 m s^-2 for 4 s. Calculate the work done by the force.
questions.explanation: Distance s = ½at^2 = ½(0.1)(4^2) = 0.8 m, so W = Fs = 40 x 0.8 = 32 J.

questions.stem: A body rolls down a slope from a height of 100 m. Its velocity at the foot of the slope is 20 m s^-1. What percentage of its initial potential energy is converted into kinetic energy? (g = 10 m s^-2)

The coefficient of static friction between a 40 kg crate and a concrete surface is 0.25. Find the magnitude of the minimum force needed to keep the crate stationary on the concrete base inclined at 45° to the horizontal. [g = 10 m s^-2]
If a beaker is filled with water, it is observed that the surface of the water is not horizontal at the glass-water interface. This behaviour is due to
questions.explanation: The curved meniscus at the glass-water boundary is caused by surface tension (adhesion of water to glass).

questions.stem: The mechanical advantage (MA) of an inclined plane depends on
options: the product of its length and height
the ratio of its length and its height
questions.explanation: For an ideal inclined plane MA = length/height, so it depends on the ratio of length to height.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A load of 5 N gives an extension of 0.56 cm in a wire which obeys Hooke's law. What is the extension caused by a load of 20 N?
questions.explanation: Extension is proportional to load: 0.56 x 20/5 = 2.24 cm.

questions.stem: A cube of side 10 cm and mass 0.5 kg floats in a liquid with only 1/5 of its height above the liquid surface. What is the relative density of the liquid?
questions.explanation: Volume submerged = 4/5 x 1000 = 800 cm^3 must displace 500 g of liquid, so density = 500/800 = 0.625.

questions.stem: The distance between the fixed points of a centigrade thermometer is 20 cm. What is the temperature when the mercury level is 4.5 cm above the lower mark?
The length of a side of a metallic cube at 20 °C is 5.0 cm. Given that the linear expansivity of the metal is 4.0 x 10^-5 K^-1, find the volume of the cube at 120 °C.

As a result of air at the top of a barometer, the height of the mercury column is 73.5 cm when it should be 75.0 cm; the volume of the space above the mercury is 8.0 cm^3. Calculate the correct barometric height when the barometer reads 74.0 cm and the volume of the space above the mercury is 6.0 cm^3.
questions.explanation: Trapped air pressure is 1.5 cmHg at 8.0 cm^3; by Boyle's law at 6.0 cm^3 it is 1.5 x 8/6 = 2.0 cmHg, so true height = 74.0 + 2.0 = 76.0 cm.

questions.stem: Hot water is added to three times its mass of water at 10 °C and the resulting temperature is 20 °C. What is the initial temperature of the hot water?
questions.explanation: Heat lost = heat gained: m(θ - 20) = 3m(20 - 10), so θ = 50 °C.

questions.stem: Calculate the amount of heat required to convert 2 kg of ice at -2 °C to water at 0 °C. (Specific heat capacity of ice = 2090 J kg^-1 °C^-1, specific latent heat of fusion = 333 kJ kg^-1).
In which of the following are the substances arranged in descending order of their thermal conductivities?
questions.explanation: Copper conducts heat better than steel, and glass is a poor conductor.

questions.stem: The vacuum in the Thermos flask helps to reduce heat transfer by
questions.explanation: Conduction and convection need a material medium, so the vacuum stops them; the silvered walls reduce radiation.

questions.stem: Which of the following phenomena explains the fact that a house whose roof is coated with white paint will be cooler in the hot season than one coated with black paint?
questions.explanation: White surfaces reflect most of the radiant heat, while black surfaces absorb it.

questions.stem: A wave has a frequency of 2 Hz and a wavelength of 30 cm. The velocity of the wave is
A boat at anchor is rocked by waves whose crests are 100 m apart and whose velocity is 25 m s^-1. At what interval does the wave crest reach the boat?
questions.explanation: Period T = λ/v = 100/25 = 4.00 s.

questions.stem: Which of the following instruments has a pure tone?
questions.explanation: A tuning fork vibrates essentially at a single frequency with no overtones, giving a pure tone.

questions.stem: The lowest note emitted by a stretched string has a frequency of 40 Hz. How many overtones are there between 40 Hz and 150 Hz?
questions.explanation: A string gives all harmonics 40, 80, 120, 160 Hz...; the overtones between 40 Hz and 150 Hz are 80 Hz and 120 Hz, i.e. 2.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements supports the assumption that light travels in straight lines?
options: A source of light produces distinct shadows of opaque objects
A source of light produces interference patterns on a suitably placed screen
questions.explanation: Sharp shadows of opaque objects are formed because light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation).

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: If an object is placed in front of two mirrors inclined at 90°, how many images will be formed?

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An object 3.0 cm high is placed 60.0 cm from a converging lens whose focal length is 20.0 cm. Calculate the size of the image formed.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/20 - 1/60 gives v = 30 cm; magnification = 30/60 = 0.5, so image height = 1.5 cm.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A pool of water appears to be 1.0 m deep when viewed vertically from above. If the refractive index of water is 1.33, what is the actual depth of the pool?
questions.explanation: Real depth = n x apparent depth = 1.33 x 1.0 = 1.330 m.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A ray of light is incident at an angle of 30° on the top surface of a parallel-sided glass block of refractive index 1.5. The ray finally emerges from the lower surface. What is the angular deviation of the emergent ray?
questions.explanation: For a parallel-sided block the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray (only laterally displaced), so the angular deviation is 0°.

questions.stem: Four lenses are being considered for use as a microscope objective. Which of the following focal lengths is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A microscope objective is a converging lens of very short focal length, e.g. +5 mm.

questions.stem: If the angle of declination in a place is 10° E, calculate the true geographic bearing if the compass reads N40°E.
questions.explanation: With easterly declination magnetic north lies 10° east of true north, so true bearing = 40° + 10° = N50°E.

questions.stem: Two capacitances of 6 μF and 8 μF are connected in series. What additional capacitance must be connected in series with this combination to give a total of 3 μF?

M and N are insulated metal spheres in contact. A negatively charged ebonite rod P is brought near M. When M and N are separated and the rod is taken away, which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: Both M and N have acquired negative charges
Both M and N have acquired positive charges
M has acquired negative charge and N positive charge
M has acquired positive charge and N negative charge
questions.explanation: By induction, electrons are repelled from M to the far sphere N, so M (near the rod) becomes positive and N negative.

questions.stem: When a transformer has more secondary windings than primary windings, it
questions.explanation: It is a step-up transformer: voltage rises, so for (at most) the same power the secondary current is smaller.

questions.stem: A current of 0.5 A flows through a resistor when connected to a 40-V battery. How much energy is dissipated in 2 minutes?
The direction of the magnetic field at a point in the vicinity of a bar magnet is
options: always towards the north pole of the magnet
always away from the south pole of the magnet
along the line joining the point to the neutral point
in the direction the north pole of a compass needle would point
questions.explanation: The field direction at a point is defined as the direction in which a free north pole (compass needle N) points.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: When two parallel wires carry currents in opposite directions, the force on either wire is
options: zero, because the currents cancel each other
twice as much as when the currents are in the same direction
questions.explanation: Antiparallel currents repel, so each wire is pushed away from the other.

questions.stem: A galvanometer of resistance 20 Ω is to be provided with a shunt so that 1/10 of the whole current in a circuit passes through the galvanometer. The resistance of the shunt is
questions.explanation: The shunt carries 9/10 of the current at the same p.d.: (I/10)(20) = (9I/10)S, so S = 20/9 = 2.22 Ω.

questions.stem: What type of reaction is represented by the following scheme? (2,1)X + (2,1)Y -> (3,2)Z + (1,0)n + energy  [nuclides written as (mass number, atomic number)]
questions.explanation: Two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus with release of energy: nuclear fusion.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE of photoelectric effect?
options: The energy of the emitted electron is independent of the work function of the surface
The energy of the emitted electron depends on the wavelength of the incident light
The greater the intensity of the incident light, the greater the energy of the emitted electron
questions.explanation: KEmax = hc/λ - W, so the electron energy depends on the wavelength (frequency) of the light, not its intensity.

questions.stem: Isotopes are nuclei which have
options: the same number of neutrons and electrons
equal number of electrons and protons
the same atomic number but different number of neutrons
the same number of total particles
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same proton (atomic) number but different neutron numbers.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample initially contains N atoms. After three half-lives the number of atoms that have disintegrated is
questions.explanation: After 3 half-lives N/8 remain, so 7N/8 have disintegrated.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the correct SI units of the quantities indicated? I. N (Force) II. N m^-1 (Torque) III. Watt (power) IV. kg m s^-2 (Momentum)
questions.explanation: Torque is measured in N m (not N m^-1) and momentum in kg m s^-1 (not kg m s^-2), so only I and III are correct.

questions.stem: A lorry travels 10 km northwards, 4 km eastwards, 6 km southwards and 4 km westwards to arrive at a point T. What is the total displacement?
questions.explanation: East and west movements cancel; net north-south displacement = 10 - 6 = 4 km north.

questions.stem: Two forces whose resultant is 100 N, are at right angles to each other. If one of them makes an angle of 30° with the resultant, determine its magnitude.
questions.explanation: The component along a direction 30° from the resultant is 100 cos 30° = 86.6 N.

questions.stem: Which of the following quantities are scalars? I. Electrical potential II. Torque III. Momentum IV. Kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Electrical potential and kinetic energy have magnitude only; torque and momentum are vectors.

questions.stem: A particle starts from rest and moves with a constant acceleration of 0.5 m s^-2. The distance covered by the particle in 10 s is
When taking a penalty kick, a footballer applies a force of 30.0 N for a period of 0.05 s. If the mass of the ball is 0.075 kg, calculate the speed with which the ball moves off.
questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum: v = Ft/m = (30 x 0.05)/0.075 = 20.00 m s^-1.

questions.stem: A 20-toothed gear wheel drives a 60-toothed one. If the angular speed of the smaller wheel is 120 rev s^-1, the angular speed of the larger wheel is
questions.explanation: Angular speeds are inversely proportional to the numbers of teeth: 120 x 20/60 = 40 rev s^-1.

questions.stem: How long will it take a 60 kg man to climb a height of 22 m if he expended energy at the rate of 0.25 kW? [g = 10 m s^-2]

A force, 10 N, drags a mass 10 kg on a horizontal table with an acceleration of 0.2 m s^-2. If the acceleration due to gravity is 10 m s^-2, the coefficient of friction between the moving mass and the table is
A body whose mass is 2 kg and has a volume of 500 cm^3 just floats when completely immersed in a liquid. Calculate the density of the liquid.
questions.explanation: It just floats fully immersed, so liquid density = body density = 2/(500 x 10^-6) = 4.0 x 10^3 kg m^-3.

questions.stem: The product PV where P is pressure and V is volume has the same unit as
questions.explanation: PV has units N m^-2 x m^3 = N m = J, the unit of energy.

questions.stem: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 10 kg of copper by 1 K is its
questions.explanation: Heat capacity is the heat needed to raise the temperature of the whole body by 1 K; specific heat capacity refers to 1 kg.

questions.stem: A tap supplies water at 25 °C while another supplies water at 75 °C. If a man wishes to bathe with water at 40 °C, the ratio of the mass of cold water to the mass of hot water required is
When heat is applied to one end of a metal rod, the molecules at the other end soon begin to vibrate with greater amplitude than before because heat has been transferred by
questions.explanation: Heat passes along a solid by molecular vibrations passed from particle to particle: conduction.

questions.stem: Which of the following media allow the transmission of sound waves through them? I. Air II. Liquids III. Solids
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and travels through gases, liquids and solids.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties is/are common to all waves? I. Diffraction II. Refraction III. Interference
questions.explanation: All waves can be reflected, refracted, diffracted and can interfere.

questions.stem: A piano wire 0.5 m long has a total mass of 0.01 kg and is stretched with a tension of 800 N. Calculate the frequency of the wire when it sounds its fundamental note.
questions.explanation: Mass per unit length μ = 0.02 kg m^-1, v = sqrt(T/μ) = 200 m s^-1, f = v/2L = 200/1 = 200 Hz.

questions.stem: A note is called an octave of another note when
options: its frequency is twice that of the first note
its frequency is half that of the first note
the notes have the same fundamental frequency
its periodic time is twice that of the first note
questions.explanation: An octave above a note has double its frequency.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors affects the speed of sound in air? I. Temperature II. Pressure III. Frequency
questions.explanation: Speed of sound in air depends on temperature; at constant temperature a change in pressure does not change it, and it is independent of frequency.

questions.stem: The speed of sound in air at sea-level is 340 m s^-1 while that of light is 300,000 km s^-1. How far (to the nearest metre) from the centre of a thunderstorm is an observer who hears a thunder 2 s after a lightning flash?
questions.explanation: Light arrives almost instantly, so distance = 340 x 2 = 680 m.

questions.stem: A slight loading of a tuning fork has the effect of
questions.explanation: Adding mass to the prongs lowers their natural frequency of vibration.

questions.stem: Two strings of the same length and under the same tension give notes of frequencies in the ratio 4 : 1. The masses of the strings are in the corresponding ratio of
questions.explanation: f is proportional to 1/sqrt(m) for the same length and tension, so m1 : m2 = (1/4)^2 = 1 : 16.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: To obtain a magnification of 2.5, how far should an object be placed from the pole of a thin converging lens of focal length 0.20 m?
questions.explanation: For a real image m = v/u = 2.5 and 1/u + 1/v = 1/f give u = f(1 + 1/m) = 0.20 x 1.4 = 0.28 m. (The focal length is printed as 10.20 m in the source, an evident misprint for 0.20 m.)

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What is the position and nature of the image formed?
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/15 - 1/10 = -1/30, so v = -30 cm: the image is 30 cm behind the mirror and virtual.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Which of the following phenomena explain the formation of a mirage? I. Reflection II. Refraction III. Diffraction
questions.explanation: A mirage is produced by refraction through air layers of varying density ending in total internal reflection.

questions.stem: When white light is dispersed by a spectrometer, the component having the shortest wavelength is
questions.explanation: Violet has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE of ultra-violet, visible and infra-red rays?
options: They are all electromagnetic waves with the same wavelength.
Ultra-violet rays have shorter wavelengths than infra-red rays and produce fluorescence.
Infra-red rays have shorter wavelength than visible light and produce the sensation of heat.
The wavelengths increase in the sequence: visible, ultra-violet, infra-red.
questions.explanation: UV has shorter wavelength than visible and IR, and causes fluorescence; IR has longer wavelength than visible light.

questions.stem: E, F and G are yellow, red and cyan transparent light filters respectively. The colour of a white opaque object when viewed through the arrangement of the filters is
questions.explanation: Yellow passes red and green, red then passes only red, and cyan (green + blue) absorbs red, so no light gets through: black.

questions.stem: A spectrum of sunlight is said to be impure when
options: it is made of only three colours
it has no red colour in it
the different colours in it overlap
it does not contain white light
questions.explanation: An impure spectrum is one in which the colours overlap instead of being separated.

questions.stem: A cell of internal resistance 2 ohms supplies current to a 6-ohm resistor. The efficiency of the cell is
questions.explanation: Efficiency = R/(R + r) = 6/8 = 75.0%.

questions.stem: When a resistance R is across a cell, the voltage across the terminals of the cell is reduced to two-thirds of its nominal value. The internal resistance of the cell is
questions.explanation: V = ER/(R + r) = 2E/3 gives 3R = 2R + 2r, so r = R/2.

questions.stem: A household refrigerator is rated 200 watts. If electricity costs 5k per kWh, what is the cost of operating it for 20 days?
questions.explanation: Energy = 0.2 kW x 24 h x 20 = 96 kWh; cost = 96 x 5k = 480k = N4.80.

questions.stem: Which of the following instruments consumes the highest current? (Instrument: voltage rating, power rating)
questions.explanation: I = P/V: iron 4 A, TV 0.5 A, torch 5 A, heater 4.55 A, so the torch light draws the most current.

questions.stem: Which of the following ammeters may be used to measure alternating current? I. Moving-coil ammeter II. Moving-iron ammeter III. Hot-wire ammeter
questions.explanation: Moving-iron and hot-wire meters respond to a.c.; a moving-coil meter only measures d.c. (without a rectifier).

questions.stem: The principle of operation of an induction coil is based on
questions.explanation: An induction coil works by electromagnetic induction, described by Faraday's law.

questions.stem: A dynamo primarily converts
questions.explanation: A dynamo (generator) converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.

questions.stem: In a certain fusion reaction, a deuteron (2,1 H) interacts with a triton (3,1 H) and produces an α-particle (4,2 He) and a second product. The second product is
questions.explanation: Mass number: 2 + 3 = 4 + 1; charge: 1 + 1 = 2 + 0, so the second product is a neutron (1,0 n).

questions.stem: Which of the following symbolic representations is correct for an atom X with 22 electrons and 43 neutrons? (Written as mass number/atomic number X)
questions.explanation: Atomic number = 22 (protons = electrons) and mass number = 22 + 43 = 65, so 65/22 X.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a set of vectors?
questions.explanation: Acceleration, velocity and moment all have direction; mass, volume and density are scalars.

questions.stem: The magnitude of the resultant of two mutually perpendicular forces, F1 and F2, is 13 N. If the magnitude of F1 is 5 N, what is the magnitude of F2?
Two points on a velocity-time graph have co-ordinates (5 s, 10 m s^-1) and (20 s, 20 m s^-1). Calculate the mean acceleration between the two points.
questions.explanation: a = Δv/Δt = (20 - 10)/(20 - 5) = 0.67 m s^-2 (the source prints the unit of option A as m s^-1).

questions.stem: A uniform circular object has centre R and diameter PS. A circular section, centre Q and diameter PR, is cut away from it. If PQRS is a straight line, where is the centre of gravity of the remaining figure?
options: A point between P and R
A point between R and S
questions.explanation: Removing mass from the P side shifts the centre of gravity away from the hole, i.e. to a point between R and S.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum of mass m moves along an arc of a circle of radius R in a vertical plane. What is the work done by gravity in a downward swing through the angle θ to 0°?
questions.explanation: The bob falls a vertical height R - R cos θ, so work done by gravity = mgR(1 - cos θ).

questions.stem: A block of mass m is held in equilibrium against a vertical wall by a horizontal force. If the coefficient of friction between the block and the wall is μ, the minimum value of the horizontal force is
questions.explanation: Friction μF must balance the weight mg, so F = mg/μ.

questions.stem: A thin film of liquid is trapped between two glass plates. The force required to pull the plates apart will increase if the
options: surface tension of the liquid is reduced
perpendicular distance between the plates is increased
area of the liquid surface in contact with the plates is increased
pressure of the air is decreased
questions.explanation: The adhesive (surface tension) force holding the plates grows with the area of liquid in contact with them.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices are used to measure pressure? I. Aneroid barometer II. Hydrometer III. Hygrometer IV. Manometer
questions.explanation: Barometers and manometers measure pressure; a hydrometer measures relative density and a hygrometer measures humidity.

questions.stem: A piece of wood of mass 40 g and uniform cross-sectional area of 2 cm^2 floats upright in water. The length of the wood immersed is
questions.explanation: It displaces 40 g = 40 cm^3 of water, so immersed length = 40/2 = 20 cm.

questions.stem: A column of air 10.0 cm long is trapped in a tube at 27 °C. What is the length of the column at 100 °C?
questions.explanation: At constant pressure L is proportional to T: L = 10.0 x 373/300 = 12.4 cm.

questions.stem: A mass of gas at 7 °C and 70 cm of mercury has a volume of 1200 cm^3. Determine its volume at 27 °C and pressure of 75 cm of mercury.

An electric heater is used to melt a block of ice, mass 1.5 kg. If the heater is powered by a 12 V battery and a current of 20 A flows through the coil, calculate the time taken to melt the block of ice at 0 °C. (Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 336 x 10^3 J kg^-1).
From the kinetic theory of gases, temperature is a
options: form of energy and is proportional to the total kinetic energy of the molecules
form of energy and is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules
physical property and is proportional to the total kinetic energy of the molecules
physical property and is proportional to the average energy of the molecules
questions.explanation: Temperature is not energy; it is a property measuring the average (kinetic) energy per molecule.

questions.stem: A vibrator of frequency 60 Hz is used in generating transverse stationary waves in a long thin wire. If the average distance between successive nodes on the wire is 45 cm, find the speed of the transverse waves in the wire.
questions.explanation: Node spacing = λ/2, so λ = 0.90 m and v = fλ = 60 x 0.90 = 54 m s^-1.

questions.stem: An air column is set into vibration by a tuning fork. In this state of resonance, the waves in the air column will be
questions.explanation: Sound in air is longitudinal, and at resonance the incident and reflected waves form a stationary wave.

questions.stem: In a sound wave in air, the adjacent rarefactions and compressions are separated by a distance of 17 cm. If the velocity of the sound wave is 340 m s^-1, determine the frequency.
questions.explanation: Adjacent compression and rarefaction are λ/2 apart, so λ = 0.34 m and f = 340/0.34 = 1000 Hz.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Light of wavelength 5000 x 10^-8 cm travels in free space with a velocity of 3 x 10^8 m s^-1. What is its wavelength in glass of refractive index 1.5?
questions.explanation: Frequency is unchanged, so λ_glass = λ/n = 5000/1.5 = 3333 x 10^-8 cm.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The magnification of the image of an object placed in front of a convex mirror is 1/3. If the radius of curvature of the mirror is 24 cm, what is the distance between the object and its image?
questions.explanation: f = -12 cm; with v = -u/3, 1/u - 3/u = -1/12 gives u = 24 cm and the virtual image 8 cm behind the mirror, so separation = 24 + 8 = 32 cm.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The plane mirrors in a kaleidoscope are usually placed
questions.explanation: Kaleidoscope mirrors are inclined at 60°, giving 360/60 - 1 = 5 images in a symmetric pattern.

questions.stem: A far sighted person cannot see objects that are less than 100 cm away. If this person wants to read a book at 25 cm, what type and focal length of lens does he need?
questions.explanation: The lens must form a virtual image at 100 cm of an object at 25 cm: 1/f = 1/25 - 1/100 = 3/100, f = +33 cm (convex).

questions.stem: When a yellow card is observed through a blue glass, the card would appear
questions.explanation: A yellow card reflects red and green light, which blue glass absorbs, so no light reaches the eye: the card looks black.

questions.stem: Dispersion of light by a glass prism is due to the
options: different hidden colours of the glass
different speeds of the various colours in glass
questions.explanation: Each colour travels at a different speed in glass, so it is refracted by a different amount.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs is NOT part of the electromagnetic spectrum? I. Radio waves II. Beta rays III. Gamma rays IV. Alpha rays
questions.explanation: Beta and alpha rays are streams of particles, not electromagnetic waves.

questions.stem: Two insulated charged spheres of different sizes and carrying opposite charges are connected together by a metallic conductor. Current will flow from one sphere to the other until both spheres
options: carry the same magnitude and sign of charge
questions.explanation: Charge flows between conductors until there is no potential difference between them.

questions.stem: A bar magnet is most effectively demagnetized by
options: placing it in a N-S position and hitting it with a hammer
subjecting it to an electric current from a battery
bringing its north pole in contact with the north pole of a very strong magnet
questions.explanation: Strong heating (above the Curie point) destroys the alignment of the magnetic domains.

questions.stem: The resistance of a 5 m uniform wire of cross-sectional area 0.2 x 10^-6 m^2 is 0.425 Ω. What is the resistivity of the material of the wire?

Three resistors, with resistances 250 Ω, 500 Ω and 1 kΩ, are connected in series. A 6 V battery is connected to either end of the combination. Calculate the potential difference between the ends of the 250 Ω resistor.
A calibrated potentiometer is used to measure the e.m.f. of a cell because the
options: internal resistance of a cell is small compared with that of the potentiometer
potentiometer takes no current from the cell
resistance of the potentiometer is less than that of a voltmeter
questions.explanation: At the balance point no current flows from the cell, so there is no lost volt and the true e.m.f. is measured.

questions.stem: The function of a 5-A fuse included in a circuit supplying a household refrigerator with power is to keep the
options: temperature of the refrigerator low and constant
current supplied to the refrigerator below 5 A
current supplied to the refrigerator constant and above 5 A
questions.explanation: The fuse melts if the current exceeds 5 A, so it keeps the current below 5 A.

questions.stem: An ammeter of resistance 0.1 ohm has a full-scale deflection of 50 mA. Determine the resultant full-scale deflection of the meter when a shunt of 0.0111 Ω is connected across its terminals.
The electrochemical equivalent of silver is 0.0012 g/C. If 36.0 g of silver is to be deposited by electrolysis on a surface by passing a steady current for 5.0 minutes, the current must be

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: A conductor PQ carries a current I. At a particular position near the conductor is a compass needle K. Neglecting the earth's magnetic field, the compass needle will
options: settle in a fixed direction only if conductor PQ is a magnetic material
settle in a fixed direction whether conductor PQ is a magnetic material or not
questions.explanation: Any current produces a magnetic field around it, so the needle aligns with that field whatever the conductor is made of.

questions.stem: When a radiation strikes a metal surface, electrons may be ejected from the metal. The maximum kinetic energy which may be acquired by an ejected electron depends on the
questions.explanation: KEmax = hc/λ - W, so it depends on wavelength (frequency), not intensity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is TRUE of the particles emitted in radioactive disintegration?
options: The alpha particle is the helium nucleus (3,2)He
The alpha particle is lighter than the beta particle
The alpha particle is deflected more than the beta particle in a magnetic field
The beta particle is deflected more than the alpha particle in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: Beta particles (electrons) have a much smaller mass, so they are deflected more; the alpha particle is (4,2)He and is far heavier.

questions.stem: Eight alpha decays and six beta decays are necessary before an atom of (238,92)U achieves stability. The final product in the chain has an atomic number of
Which of the following is a fundamental unit?
questions.explanation: The second is an SI base (fundamental) unit; newton, watt and joule are derived units.

questions.stem: A car moving with a speed of 90 km h^-1 was brought uniformly to rest by the application of the brakes in 10 s. How far did the car travel after the brakes were applied?
questions.explanation: 90 km h^-1 = 25 m s^-1; distance = average speed x time = (25/2) x 10 = 125 m.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are correct about an object in equilibrium under parallel forces? I. The total clockwise moments of the forces about any point equals the total anticlockwise moments about the same point. II. The total forces in one direction equals the total forces in the opposite direction. III. The resolved components along the x-axis equals the resolved component along the y-axis.
questions.explanation: Equilibrium under parallel forces requires zero resultant force and zero resultant moment; III is not a condition.

questions.stem: A stone of mass m kg is held h metres above the floor for 50 s. The work done in joules over the period is
questions.explanation: The stone does not move, so no work is done.

questions.stem: A body of mass 10 kg rests on a rough inclined plane whose angle of tilt θ is variable. θ is gradually increased until the body starts to slide down the plane at 30°. The coefficient of limiting friction between the body and the plane is
questions.explanation: At the point of sliding μ = tan θ = tan 30° = 0.58.

questions.stem: An inclined plane which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal has a velocity ratio of
questions.explanation: VR = 1/sin θ = 1/sin 30° = 2.

questions.stem: What is the length of the liquid column in a barometer tube that would support an atmospheric pressure of 102000 N m^-2 if the density of the liquid is 2600 kg m^-3? [g = 10 m s^-2].
