40 cm^3 of liquid P is mixed with 60 cm^3 of another liquid Q. If the densities of P and Q are 1.00 kg m^-3 and 1.6 kg m^-3 respectively, what is the density of the mixture?
questions.explanation: Density = total mass/total volume = (40 x 1.00 + 60 x 1.6)/100 = 1.36.

questions.stem: The resistances of a platinum wire at the ice and steam points are 0.75 ohm and 1.05 ohm respectively. Determine the temperature at which the resistance of the wire is 0.90 ohm.
A bar of initial length l0 is heated through a temperature change Δt to a new length l. The linear expansivity, α, of the bar is
questions.explanation: α = increase in length/(original length x temperature change) = (l - l0)/(l0 Δt).

questions.stem: The pressure of a gas when cooled at constant volume will decrease because the molecules
options: collide less frequently with the walls of the container
have the same average kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Cooling lowers molecular speeds, so molecules hit the walls less often and less hard, reducing pressure.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions will make water boil at a temperature of 100 °C when the atmospheric pressure is 750 mm Hg?
options: Heat more rapidly at the same pressure
Reduce the external pressure by a quarter
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C at 760 mmHg; at 750 mmHg it boils below 100 °C, so the external pressure must be raised.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are correct? I. Land and sea breezes are natural convection currents. II. Convection may occur in liquids or gases but not in solids. III. The vacuum in a thermos flask prevents heat loss due to convection only.
questions.explanation: The vacuum stops both conduction and convection, so III is wrong; I and II are correct.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A light wave of frequency 5 x 10^14 Hz moves through water which has a refractive index of 4/3. Calculate the wavelength in water if the velocity of light in air is 3 x 10^8 m s^-1.
A wave disturbance travelling in air enters a medium in which its velocity is less than that in air. Which of the following statements is true about the wave in the medium?
options: Both the frequency of the wave and the wavelength are decreased.
The frequency of the wave is decreased while the wavelength is increased.
The frequency of the wave is unaltered while the wavelength is decreased.
The frequency of the wave is decreased while the wavelength is unaltered.
questions.explanation: Frequency is fixed by the source; since v = fλ, a lower speed means a shorter wavelength.

questions.stem: Shadows and eclipses result from the
questions.explanation: Shadows and eclipses form because light travels in straight lines.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An object which is 3 cm high is placed vertically 10 cm in front of a concave mirror. If this object produces an image 40 cm from the mirror, the height of the image is
questions.explanation: Magnification = v/u = 40/10 = 4, so image height = 4 x 3 = 12.00 cm.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A boy looks at the image of an object in a plane mirror. He observes two images, a main bright one and the other faint. The observed images result from
questions.explanation: Light is refracted into the glass of the mirror and reflected at both the front surface and the silvered back, giving a faint and a bright image.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: What must be the distance between an object and a converging lens of focal length 20 cm to produce an erect image two times the object height?
questions.explanation: An erect image is virtual with v = -2u: 1/u - 1/(2u) = 1/20 gives u = 10 cm.

questions.stem: For a short sighted person, light rays from a point on a very distant object are focused
options: on the retina by a converging lens
behind the retina by a diverging lens
in front of the retina a distance 2F from the lens
questions.explanation: In myopia the eye is too strongly converging, so distant objects are focused in front of the retina.

questions.stem: When light is incident on an object which is magenta in colour, which of the following colours will be absorbed?
questions.explanation: Magenta reflects red and blue and absorbs green.

questions.stem: One of the properties of the earth's magnetic field is that the
options: north pole lies in the northern hemisphere
earth's magnetic flux is entirely horizontal at a place where the magnetic dip is zero
earth's magnetic flux is entirely vertical at a place where the magnetic dip is zero
questions.explanation: Zero dip (magnetic equator) means the field has no vertical component, so it is entirely horizontal.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are true of an insulated charged body carrying a positive charge? I. It contains excess positive charges II. It creates an electric field III. It possesses potential energy IV. It carries electric current.
questions.explanation: A static charged body has excess charge, sets up a field and has electrical potential energy, but no current flows in it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a vector?
questions.explanation: Electric field intensity has both magnitude and direction.

questions.stem: Three cells each of e.m.f. 1.5 V and an internal resistance of 1.0 Ω are connected in parallel across a load resistance of 2.67 Ω. Calculate the current in the load.
questions.explanation: In parallel E = 1.5 V and r = 1/3 Ω, so I = 1.5/(2.67 + 0.33) = 0.50 A.

questions.stem: When a known standard resistor of 2.0 Ω is connected to the 0.0 cm end of a metre bridge the balance point is found to be 55.0 cm. What is the value of the unknown resistor?
The total energy required to send a unit positive charge round a complete electrical circuit is the
questions.explanation: E.m.f. is the total work done per unit charge in driving charge round the complete circuit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an essential physical property of the wires used for making fuses?
questions.explanation: A fuse wire must melt readily when the current exceeds its rating, so it needs a low melting point.

questions.stem: Electrical power is transmitted at a high voltage rather than low voltage because the amount of energy loss is reduced due to
questions.explanation: At high voltage the current is small, so the I^2R heat dissipated in the lines is reduced.

questions.stem: A lamp is rated 240 V, 60 W. The resistance of the filament is
A 0 - 10 mA galvanometer with a coil resistance of 30 Ω can be converted to a 0 - 10 A ammeter by using
questions.explanation: Shunt S = IgRg/(I - Ig) = (0.01 x 30)/9.99 ≈ 0.03 Ω, connected in parallel.

questions.stem: The number of neutrons contained in the nucleus of (238,92)U is
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 238 - 92 = 146.

questions.stem: What precaution should a manufacturer take to ensure that energy loss in a transformer is minimized?
options: The winding of the transformer should be made of high resistance wires.
The core should be made of thin sheets of metal.
No magnetic material should be used to make the core.
The flux linking the primary with the secondary coils should be minimum.
questions.explanation: A laminated core of thin insulated sheets reduces eddy-current losses.

questions.stem: A substance has a half life of 3 min. After 6 min, the count rate was observed to be 400. What was its count rate at zero time?
questions.explanation: 6 min is two half-lives, so the initial rate = 400 x 2^2 = 1600.

questions.stem: The photocell works on the principle of the
options: emission of electrons by incident radiation
emission of protons by incident electrons
questions.explanation: A photocell relies on the photoelectric effect: radiation falling on a metal ejects electrons.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most suitable for use as an altimeter?
questions.explanation: An aneroid barometer is portable and can be calibrated directly in height, so it is used as an altimeter.

questions.stem: A body of weight W N rests on a smooth plane inclined at an angle θ° to the horizontal. What is the resolved part of the weight in newtons along the plane?
questions.explanation: The component of the weight along the incline is W sin θ (W cos θ is perpendicular to it).

questions.stem: A small metal ball is thrown vertically upwards from the top of a tower with an initial velocity of 20 m s^-1. If the ball took a total of 6 s to reach ground level, determine the height of the tower.
questions.explanation: Taking g = 10 m s^-2: s = ut - ½gt^2 = 20(6) - 5(36) = -60 m, so the tower is 60 m high.

questions.stem: An object moves with uniform speed round a circle. Its acceleration has
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration v^2/r has constant size but always points to the centre, so its direction changes.

questions.stem: A body of mass 100 g moving with a velocity of 10.0 m s^-1 collides with a wall. If after the collision, it moves with a velocity of 2.0 m s^-1 in the opposite direction, calculate the change in momentum.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A spring of force constant 1500 N m^-1 is acted upon by a constant force of 75 N. Calculate the potential energy stored in the spring.
A wheel and axle have radii 80 cm and 10 cm respectively. If the efficiency of the machine is 0.85, an applied force of 1200 N to the wheel will raise a load of

A body is under the action of a force F such that the force-displacement graph of the body is a semicircle (rising from F = 0 at 0 m to a maximum of 12 N at 12 m and returning to 0 at 24 m). The work done on the body by the force in moving through 24 metres is
questions.explanation: Work = area under the graph = area of a semicircle of radius 12 = ½π(12)^2 = 72π J.

questions.stem: A 20 kg mass is to be pulled up a slope inclined at 30° to the horizontal. If the efficiency of the plane is 75%, the force required to pull the load up the plane is
questions.explanation: Ideal effort = mg sin 30° = 200 x 0.5 = 100 N (g = 10 m s^-2); actual effort = 100/0.75 = 133.3 N.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: The spiral spring of a spring balance is 25.0 cm long when 5 N hangs on it and 30.0 cm long when the weight is 10 N. What is the length of the spring if the weight is 3 N assuming Hooke's Law is obeyed?
questions.explanation: Extension is 1 cm per N, so the natural length is 20.0 cm and with 3 N the length is 23.0 cm.

questions.stem: The mass of a stone is 15.0 g when completely immersed in water and 10.0 g when completely immersed in a liquid of relative density 2.0. The mass of the stone in air is
questions.explanation: m - V = 15 and m - 2V = 10 give V = 5 cm^3 and m = 20.0 g.

questions.stem: In which of the following is surface tension important?
options: The floating of a ship in water
The floating of a dry needle in water
The floating of a balloon in air
The diffusion of a sugar solution across a membrane
questions.explanation: A dry needle is supported by the surface film (surface tension), not by buoyancy.

questions.stem: A thermometer with an arbitrary scale, S, of equal divisions registers -30 °S at the ice point and +90 °S at the steam point. Calculate the Celsius temperature corresponding to 60 °S.
A brass rod is 2 m long at a certain temperature. What is the length for a temperature rise of 100 K, if the expansivity of brass is 18 x 10^-6 K^-1?

What is the difference in the amount of heat given out by 4 kg of steam and 4 kg of water when both are cooled from 100 °C to 80 °C? [The specific latent heat of steam is 2,260,000 J kg^-1, specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1]
questions.explanation: Both give out the same heat cooling as water from 100 °C to 80 °C; the steam additionally gives out mL = 4 x 2,260,000 = 9,040,000 J.

questions.stem: How long does it take a 750-W heater to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water from 20 °C to 50 °C? [Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1]
The absolute temperature of a perfect gas is proportional to the average
questions.explanation: Kinetic theory gives ½m<c^2> = (3/2)kT, so T is proportional to the average kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A room is heated by means of a charcoal fire. An occupant of the room standing away from the fire is warmed mainly by
questions.explanation: Heat from the glowing fire reaches a person standing to the side mainly as radiant (infra-red) energy.

questions.stem: A boy timed 30 oscillations of a certain pendulum thrice and obtained 1 min 10 s, 1 min 12 s and 1 min 7 s respectively. The mean period of oscillation of the pendulum is
questions.explanation: Mean time = (70 + 72 + 67)/3 = 69.67 s for 30 oscillations, so T = 69.67/30 = 2.32 s.

questions.stem: Which of the following is TRUE of light and sound waves?
options: They both need a medium for propagation
Their velocities in air are equal
questions.explanation: All waves transfer energy; light needs no medium, is transverse and is far faster than sound.

questions.stem: The image in a pin-hole camera is
options: erect and formed by refraction through a lens
erect and gets sharper as the hole becomes larger
inverted and formed by the light from each point travelling in a straight line
questions.explanation: Light from each point travels in a straight line through the hole, giving a real inverted image.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: When a plane mirror at which a ray is incident is rotated through an angle θ, the reflected ray will be rotated through
questions.explanation: Rotating a plane mirror through θ turns the reflected ray through 2θ.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A trough 12.0 cm deep is filled with water of refractive index 4/3. By how much would a coin at the bottom of the trough appear to be displaced when viewed vertically from above the water surface?
questions.explanation: Apparent depth = 12/(4/3) = 9.0 cm, so the coin appears raised by 12.0 - 9.0 = 3.0 cm.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: In a ray diagram for a thin converging lens, a ray that is not parallel to the optic axis but passes through the optical centre will
options: pass through the centre of curvature after refraction
emerge parallel to the principal axis
pass through the principal focus after refraction
questions.explanation: A ray through the optical centre of a thin lens is not deviated.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the image of an object, 4 cm from a diverging lens of focal length -12 cm?
options: The image is virtual, 3 cm in front of the lens
The image is real, 6 cm behind the lens
The image is virtual, 6 cm in front of the lens
The image is real, 3 cm in front of the lens
questions.explanation: 1/v = -1/12 - 1/4 = -1/3, so v = -3 cm: a virtual image 3 cm from the lens on the object side.

questions.stem: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded close to each other. What is the frequency of the beats produced?
questions.explanation: Beat frequency = 260 - 256 = 4 Hz.

questions.stem: A man hears his echo from a nearby hill 2 s after he shouted. If the frequency of his voice is 260 Hz and the wavelength is 1.29 m, how far away is the hill?
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 260 x 1.29 = 335.4 m s^-1; the sound goes there and back, so d = 335.4 x 2/2 = 335.4 m.

questions.stem: When the bottom tip of a vibrating tuning fork is held in contact with a wooden box, a louder sound is heard. This phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation: The box is set into (forced/resonant) vibration by the fork, so a louder sound is heard: resonance.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about the earth's magnetic field?
options: The angle of dip is the angle which a freely suspended magnet makes with the vertical
The angle of declination is the angle between the magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian
The angle of declination is the angle which a magnetic compass makes with the magnetic meridian
The angle of inclination is the difference between the angle of dip and the angle of declination
questions.explanation: Declination is the angle between the magnetic and geographic meridians; dip is measured from the horizontal.

questions.stem: An insulated rod when rubbed with a material acquires
options: a negative charge if it is made of glass and rubbed with silk
no charge if it is made of glass and rubbed with fur
no charge if it is made of copper and rubbed with silk
a positive charge if it is made of copper and rubbed with fur
questions.explanation: Copper is a conductor, so any charge produced by rubbing leaks away; glass rubbed with silk becomes positive.

questions.stem: The function of the system of granulated carbon mixed with manganese (IV) oxide in a Leclanche cell is to
options: increase the e.m.f. of the cell to 2.0 V
prevent local action in the cell
make the cell black and hence a good radiator
questions.explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide is a depolarizer: it oxidizes the hydrogen formed at the carbon rod, preventing polarization.

questions.stem: A moving coil galvanometer of 300 Ω resistance gives full scale deflection for 1.0 mA. The resistance, R, of the shunt that is required to convert the galvanometer into a 3.0 A ammeter is
Which of the following obeys Ohm's Law?
questions.explanation: Metallic conductors at constant temperature obey Ohm's law; diodes and many electrolytes do not.

questions.stem: An equipment whose power is 1500 W and resistance is 375 ohms would draw a current of
To convert an alternating current dynamo into a direct current dynamo, the
options: number of turns in the coil is increased
strength of the field magnet is increased
slip rings are replaced with a split ring commutator
coil is wound on a soft iron armature
questions.explanation: A split-ring commutator reverses the coil connections every half-turn, giving unidirectional (d.c.) output.

questions.stem: If a current carrying coil is mounted on a metal frame, the back e.m.f. induced in the coil causes
questions.explanation: The changing flux induces circulating eddy currents in the metal frame.

questions.stem: The electrochemical equivalent of platinum is 5.0 x 10^-7 kg C^-1. To plate out 1.0 kg of platinum, a current of 100 A must be passed through an appropriate vessel for

Which of the following statements are TRUE of isotopes? I. Isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons. II. Isotopes of elements are normally separated using physical properties. III. Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons in the nuclei.
questions.explanation: Isotopes have equal proton (and electron) numbers, hence identical chemistry, and are separated by physical (mass-dependent) methods.

questions.stem: When an atom loses or gains a charge, it becomes
questions.explanation: An atom that has gained or lost electrons is an ion.

questions.stem: 4 g of a radioactive material of half-life 10 days is spilled on a laboratory floor. How long would it take to disintegrate 3.5 g of the material?
questions.explanation: 0.5 g remains = 4/8 of the original, i.e. 3 half-lives = 30 days.

questions.stem: In a nuclear fusion process, four protons each of mass Mp were fused to produce a nucleus X of mass Mx. Which of the following equations is CORRECT?
questions.explanation: Energy is released in fusion, so there is a mass defect: the product is lighter than the four protons.

questions.stem: Which of the following are TRUE for α-decay? I. Mass number decreases by four II. Atomic number decreases by two III. Mass number does not change.
questions.explanation: Emitting an alpha particle (4,2)He reduces mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2.

questions.stem: Which of the following phenomena is called photoelectric effect?
options: High energy electrons impinge on a metallic anode which then emits photons
A high energy photon emits photons as it is slowed down
A metal absorbs quanta of light and then emits electrons
Two electrons are created from a quantum of light
questions.explanation: In the photoelectric effect a metal absorbs photons and emits electrons.

questions.stem: What is the least possible error in using a rule graduated in centimetres?
questions.explanation: The least possible error is half the smallest division: 1 cm / 2 = 0.5 cm.

questions.stem:
Which of the following affects the period of a simple pendulum?
I. Mass of the pendulum bob
II. Length of the pendulum
III. Acceleration due to gravity
questions.explanation: T = 2*pi*sqrt(l/g), so the period depends on the length and g but not on the mass of the bob.

questions.stem: A boy sits in a train moving with uniform speed on a straight track. If from his outstretched palm he gently tosses a coin vertically upwards, the coin will fall
questions.explanation: The coin shares the train's uniform horizontal velocity, so relative to the boy it moves straight up and down and lands back in his palm.

questions.stem: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration of 6 m s^-2. What distance does it cover in the third second?
questions.explanation: Distance in the nth second = u + a(2n - 1)/2 = 0 + 6(5)/2 = 15 m.

questions.stem: A stone, Q, is thrown with velocity u at an angle of 75° to the horizontal. Another stone R is thrown with the same velocity u but at an angle of 15° to the horizontal. The ranges covered by the stones will be
options: the same for Q and R
greater for the heavier of the stones
questions.explanation: R = u^2 sin(2θ)/g and sin 150° = sin 30°, so complementary angles give equal ranges.

questions.stem: A man weighing 800 N climbs up a flight of stairs to a height of 15 m in 12.5 s. What is the man's average power output?
A machine requires 1000 J of work to raise a load of 500 N through a vertical distance of 1.5 m. Calculate the efficiency of the machine.
questions.explanation: Efficiency = work output/work input = (500 x 1.5)/1000 = 75%.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: In an experiment to determine Young's modulus for a wire, several loads are attached to the wire and the corresponding extensions measured. The tensile stress in each case depends on the
options: load and the radius of the wire
radius of the wire and the extension
extension and the original length of the wire
questions.explanation: Tensile stress = force/cross-sectional area = load/(pi r^2), so it depends on the load and the radius.

questions.stem: If a plastic sphere floats in water (density = 1000 kg m^-3) with 0.5 of its volume submerged and floats in oil with 0.4 of its volume submerged, the density of the oil is
questions.explanation: Weight = upthrust in both: 0.5 x 1000 = 0.4 x ρ, so ρ = 1250 kg m^-3.

questions.stem: A platinum resistance thermometer wire has a resistance of 5 ohms at 0 °C and 5.5 ohms at 100 °C. Calculate the temperature of the wire when the resistance is 5.2 ohms.

A bridge made of steel is 600 m long. What is the daily variation in its length if the night-time and day-time temperatures are 10 °C and 35 °C respectively? The linear expansivity of steel is 0.000012 °C^-1.
One of the most important applications of a bimetallic strip is found in the construction of
questions.explanation: Unequal expansion bends a bimetallic strip, which makes or breaks the circuit in a thermostat.

questions.stem: At constant pressure, the density of a fixed mass of gas is
questions.explanation: At constant pressure V ∝ T (Charles' law) and density = m/V, so density ∝ 1/T.

questions.stem: How much heat is absorbed when a block of copper of mass 0.05 kg and specific heat capacity 390 J kg^-1 K^-1 is heated from 20 °C to 70 °C?
A block of ice floats on water inside a container. If the block of ice gets completely melted, the level of water in the container will
questions.explanation: Floating ice displaces its own weight of water; when it melts it produces exactly that volume of water, so the level is unchanged.

questions.stem: The space between the double glass walls of a thermos flask is evacuated and the two surfaces facing the evacuated space are silvered. The residual source of heat loss takes place by
options: conduction through the stopper and the glass
questions.explanation: The vacuum stops conduction and convection across the walls and silvering cuts radiation, leaving conduction through the stopper and the glass neck.

questions.stem: The equation of a wave is y = 0.005 sin[π(0.5x - 200t)], where x and y are in metres and t is in seconds. What is the velocity of the wave?
questions.explanation: For y = A sin(kx - ωt), v = ω/k = 200π/0.5π = 400 m s^-1.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics of a wave is used in the measurement of the depth of the sea?
questions.explanation: Echo sounding times a pulse reflected from the sea bed.

questions.stem: A note is the octave of another note if it has
options: a frequency twice that of the first note
a frequency half that of the first note
the same frequency as the first one
a frequency eight times that of the first note
questions.explanation: The octave of a note has double its frequency.

questions.stem: What is the frequency of the sound made by a siren having a disc with 32 holes and making 25 revolutions per second?
questions.explanation: f = holes x revolutions per second = 32 x 25 = 800 Hz.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem:
Which of the following properties make the convex mirror useful as a driving mirror?
I. The image is real
II. The image is erect
III. It has a wide field of view
IV. The image is magnified
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives an erect, virtual, diminished image with a wide field of view.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: When an object is placed very close to the pole of a concave mirror, the virtual image obtained is
questions.explanation: An object inside the focal length of a concave mirror gives a virtual, upright, magnified image.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 36 cm. At what distance from the mirror should an object be placed to give a real image three times the size of the object?
questions.explanation: f = 18 cm and v = 3u: 1/u + 1/(3u) = 1/18 gives u = 24 cm.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about a long-sighted boy who does not put on glasses?
options: He cannot see distant objects clearly
Rays of light from close objects are focused in front of his retina
Parallel rays of light are focused behind his retina
questions.explanation: In long sight the eyeball is too short (or the lens too weak), so rays are brought to a focus behind the retina.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The speed of light in air is 3 x 10^8 m s^-1. What is the speed in glass with a refractive index of 1.50?

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: If the refractive index of a medium in air is 2.0, what is the critical angle for this medium?
Which of the following arrangements of the components of the electromagnetic spectrum is in ascending order of wavelengths?
options: Gamma rays, ultraviolet rays, x-rays, infra-red rays
Gamma rays, x-rays, ultraviolet rays, infra-red rays
Infra-red rays, ultraviolet rays, x-rays, gamma rays
Gamma rays, ultraviolet rays, infra-red rays, x-rays
questions.explanation: Wavelength increases from gamma rays to x-rays to ultraviolet to infra-red.

questions.stem: The angle between the direction of the earth's magnetic field and the horizontal is called the
questions.explanation: The angle of dip (inclination) is the angle the earth's field makes with the horizontal.

questions.stem: Calculate the force acting on an electron of charge 1.6 x 10^-19 C placed in an electric field of intensity 10^8 V m^-1.
When an ebonite rod is rubbed with fur, it has
questions.explanation: Electrons pass from the fur to the ebonite, leaving the ebonite negatively charged.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors has no effect on the e.m.f. of a primary cell?
questions.explanation: The e.m.f. depends on the chemicals (plates and electrolyte) and temperature, not on the cell's size.

questions.stem: A wire of length 15 m made of a material of resistivity 1.8 x 10^-6 ohm-m has a resistance of 0.27 ohms. Determine the area of the wire.
A 5-V battery is connected across the plates of a 2.0 μF uncharged parallel plate capacitor. The charge on the capacitor after a long time is
questions.explanation: Q = CV = 2.0 μF x 5 V = 10 μC.

questions.stem: Which of the following apparatus will require the smallest fuse rating for its protection?
questions.explanation: I = P/V: 0.25 A, 1.5 A, 3.3 A and 8 A; the 60 W, 240 V device draws least current.

questions.stem: A capacitor of 10 μF is connected across a cell of 12 volts. Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor.
The heat produced in a conductor carrying an electric current is
options: inversely proportional to the current and the resistance
directly proportional to the current, resistance and the time
inversely proportional to the square of the resistance, current and the time
directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time
questions.explanation: Joule's law: H = I^2Rt.

questions.stem: The maximum permissible current through a galvanometer G of internal resistance 10 Ω is 0.05 A. A resistance R is used to convert G into a voltmeter with a maximum reading of 100 V. Find the value of R and how it is connected to G.
questions.explanation: A voltmeter needs a series multiplier: R = V/I - r = 100/0.05 - 10 = 1990 Ω.

questions.stem: In alternating current theory, the units of impedance, r.m.s. voltage and resonance frequency are respectively
questions.explanation: Impedance is in ohms, voltage in volts and frequency in hertz.

questions.stem: In a.c. circuit theory, the root mean square (r.m.s.) current, Irms, and the peak (maximum) current, I0, are related by
questions.explanation: For a sinusoidal current Irms = I0/sqrt(2) ≈ 0.707 I0.

questions.stem: The threshold frequency for the photoelectric effect depends on the
options: potential difference between the cathode and the anode
questions.explanation: Threshold frequency f0 = W/h is fixed by the work function of the cathode material.

questions.stem: After three half-lives, the fraction of a radioactive material that has decayed is
questions.explanation: Remaining = (1/2)^3 = 1/8, so 7/8 has decayed.

questions.stem: Which of the following quantities has the same unit as the watt?
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = force x distance/time = force x velocity.

questions.stem: The external and internal diameters of a tube are measured as (32 ± 2) mm and (21 ± 1) mm respectively. Determine the percentage error in the thickness of the tube.
Two forces of magnitudes 7 N and 3 N act at right angles to each other. The angle θ between the resultant and the 7 N force is given by
questions.explanation: The resultant is the diagonal of the right-angled rectangle, so tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 3/7.

questions.stem: An aeroplane lands on a runway at a speed of 180 km h^-1 and is brought to a stop uniformly in 30 seconds. What distance does it cover on the runway before coming to rest?
A rocket burns fuel at the rate of 10 kg s^-1 and ejects it with a velocity of 5 x 10^3 m s^-1. The thrust exerted by the gas on the rocket is
questions.explanation: Thrust = rate of change of momentum = 10 x 5 x 10^3 = 5.0 x 10^4 N.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the energy changes in the generation of light by a hydroelectric power station?
questions.explanation: Stored water's potential energy turns the turbines (mechanical), which drive generators (electrical) to power lamps (light).

questions.stem: A plane inclined at angle θ has a velocity ratio of 10 : 1. The inclination of the plane to the horizontal is given by
questions.explanation: For an inclined plane V.R. = 1/sin θ, so sin θ = 1/10.

questions.stem: A weightless vessel of dimensions 4 m x 3 m x 2 m is filled with a liquid of density 1000 kg m^-3 and sealed. What is the maximum pressure this container can exert on a flat surface? [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: Weight = 24 x 1000 x 10 = 2.4 x 10^5 N; on the smallest face (3 m x 2 m = 6 m^2), p = 2.4 x 10^5/6 = 4 x 10^4 N m^-2.

questions.stem: An object of mass 400 g and density 600 kg m^-3 is suspended with a string so that half of it is immersed in paraffin of density 900 kg m^-3. The tension in the string is [g = 10 m s^-2]
The thermometric property of the thermocouple is that its
questions.explanation: A thermocouple produces a thermoelectric e.m.f. that varies with the temperature difference between its junctions.

questions.stem: When the volume of a given mass of gas is halved and its temperature doubled, the pressure
questions.explanation: p ∝ T/V, so p becomes 2/(1/2) = 4 times the original.

questions.stem: 200 g of water at 90 °C is mixed with 100 g of water at 30 °C. What is the final temperature?
The melting point of a solid is given as 80 °C. If 10^5 J of heat energy is required at this temperature to melt 10 g of the solid, the specific latent heat of fusion of the solid is
Which of the following waves can propagate through a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Infra-red is electromagnetic and needs no medium; all the others are sound waves.

questions.stem: If the focal length of a camera lens is 20 cm, the distance from the film at which the lens must be set to produce a sharp image of an object 100 cm away is

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem:
Which of the following may be used to explain a mirage?
I. Layers of air near the road surface have varying refractive indices in hot weather
II. Road surfaces sometimes become good reflectors in hot weather
III. Light from the sky can be reflected upwards after coming close to the road surface
questions.explanation: Hot air layers of decreasing refractive index bend sky light until it is totally internally reflected upwards; the road itself does not become a reflector.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A beam of light is incident from air to water at an angle of 30°. Find the angle of refraction if the refractive index of water is 4/3.
The property of the eye known as its power of accommodation is controlled by the
questions.explanation: The ciliary muscles change the thickness, and so the focal length, of the eye lens.

questions.stem:
Which of the following correctly explain(s) why a green leaf appears green in bright daylight?
I. It absorbs only the green component of sunlight.
II. It absorbs all colours in sunlight except green.
III. It reflects only the green component of sunlight.
questions.explanation: A green surface absorbs all other colours and reflects only green.

questions.stem: The field that results from the contact of a positively charged ball with the inner wall of an uncharged hollow conducting sphere is
options: on the surface of the ball
questions.explanation: On contact the charge moves entirely to the outer surface of the hollow conductor, so the field exists only outside it.

questions.stem:
Which of the following correctly explain(s) why soft iron is preferred to steel in electromagnets?
I. Soft iron is more readily magnetized than steel.
II. Soft iron is more readily demagnetized than steel.
III. Soft iron retains magnetism more than steel.
questions.explanation: Soft iron magnetizes and demagnetizes easily (low retentivity), so the electromagnet can be switched on and off.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: A current-carrying conductor experiences a force when placed in a magnetic field because the
options: magnetic field of the current interacts with the external magnetic field
force is due to the motor principle
electric field of the current interacts with the external magnetic field
questions.explanation: The current sets up its own magnetic field, which interacts with the external field to give the force.

questions.stem: A simple cell with a mercury-amalgamated zinc electrode prevents
questions.explanation: Amalgamating the zinc keeps impurities from forming tiny local cells, preventing local action.

questions.stem: The terminal voltage of a battery is 4.0 V when supplying a current of 2.0 A, and 2.0 V when supplying a current of 3.0 A. The internal resistance of the battery is
questions.explanation: E - 2r = 4 and E - 3r = 2, so r = 2.0 Ω (and E = 8 V).

questions.stem: A current of 100 mA passes through a conductor for 2 minutes. The quantity of electricity transported is
A 40-W instrument has a resistance of 90 ohms. On what voltage should it be operated normally?
questions.explanation: P = V^2/R gives V = sqrt(40 x 90) = 60 V.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices may be used to step up the voltage in a d.c. circuit?
questions.explanation: An induction coil uses a make-and-break to produce a high voltage from a d.c. source; a transformer works only with a.c.

questions.stem: The primary aim in high tension transmission is to
options: minimize electrical energy losses due to heat production
increase the rate of energy transfer by using high voltage
increase the current in the wires
generate electricity at high current and low voltage
questions.explanation: Transmitting at high voltage means low current, so I^2R heat losses in the lines are small.

questions.stem: Determine the inductive reactance when a 30.0 mH inductor with a negligible resistance is connected to a 1.30 x 10^3 Hz oscillator.

Which of the following statements correctly describe(s) cathode rays?
I. They consist of tiny particles carrying negative electric charges
II. They are deflected in a magnetic field but not in an electric field
III. They consist of fast moving neutrons and are deflected in an electric field
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, deflected by both electric and magnetic fields.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are produced after a nuclear fusion process?
I. One heavy nucleus
II. Neutrons
III. Protons
IV. Energy
questions.explanation: In fusion light nuclei combine into one heavier nucleus, releasing energy.

questions.stem: An element X of atomic number 88 and mass number 226 decays to form an element Z by emitting two beta particles and an alpha particle. Z is represented by
options: Z with mass number 222 and atomic number 82
Z with mass number 222 and atomic number 88
Z with mass number 226 and atomic number 86
Z with mass number 226 and atomic number 80
questions.explanation: An alpha lowers A by 4 and Z by 2 (222, 86); two betas raise Z by 2, giving mass number 222 and atomic number 88.

questions.stem: The kinetic energy of a photoelectron liberated from a metallic surface depends on the
options: time duration of the incident radiation
questions.explanation: Einstein's equation: KEmax = hf - W, which depends on frequency, not intensity.

questions.stem: An object is projected with a velocity of 80 m s^-1 at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. The maximum height reached is [g = 10 m s^-2]
A motor vehicle is brought to rest from a speed of 15 m s^-1 in 20 seconds. Calculate the retardation.
Which of the following is TRUE of a particle moving in a horizontal circle with constant angular velocity?
options: The energy is constant but the linear momentum varies
The linear momentum is constant but the energy varies
Both energy and linear momentum are constant
The speed and the linear velocity are both constant
questions.explanation: The speed (and so kinetic energy) is constant, but the direction of the velocity, and hence the momentum, keeps changing.

questions.stem: A uniform wood of weight 200 N and length 50 m is pivoted at one end and suspended by a cord at the other end at an angle of 30° to the wood. Calculate the tension in the cord if the wood is horizontal.
questions.explanation: Moments about the pivot: T sin 30° x 50 = 200 x 25, so T = 200 N.

questions.stem: An object of mass 50 kg is released from a height of 2 m. Find the kinetic energy just before it strikes the ground. [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: KE = loss of PE = mgh = 50 x 10 x 2 = 1000 J.

questions.stem: Calculate the magnitude of the force required to just move a 20 kg object along a horizontal surface if the coefficient of friction is 0.2. [g = 10 m s^-2]

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A spring of length 25 cm is extended to 30 cm by a load of 150 N attached to one of its ends. What is the energy stored in the spring?

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A force of 15 N stretches a spring to a total length of 30 cm. An additional force of 10 N stretches the spring 5 cm further. Find the natural length of the spring.
questions.explanation: k = 10 N/5 cm = 2 N/cm; 15 N gives 7.5 cm extension, so natural length = 30 - 7.5 = 22.5 cm.

questions.stem:
Which of these statements are TRUE of pressure in liquids?
I. Pressure acts equally in all directions.
II. Pressure decreases with depth.
III. Pressure at the same level of a liquid is the same.
IV. Pressure is dependent on the cross-sectional area of the barometer tube.
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure acts equally in all directions and is the same at the same level; it increases with depth and does not depend on the area.

questions.stem: The mass of a specific gravity bottle is 15.2 g when it is empty. It is 24.8 g when filled with kerosene and 27.2 g when filled with distilled water. Calculate the relative density of kerosene.
If a solid X floats in liquid P of relative density 2.0 and in liquid Q of relative density 1.5, it can be inferred that the
options: weight of P displaced is greater than that of Q
weight of P displaced is less than that of Q
volume of P displaced is greater than that of Q
volume of P displaced is less than that of Q
questions.explanation: A floating body displaces its own weight in both liquids, so it displaces a smaller volume of the denser liquid P.

questions.stem: A motor tyre is inflated to a pressure of 2.0 x 10^5 N m^-2 when the temperature of the air is 27 °C. What will be the pressure in it at 87 °C, assuming that the volume of the tyre does not change?
When 100 g of liquid L1 at 78 °C was mixed with X g of liquid L2 at 50 °C, the final temperature was 66 °C. Given that the specific heat capacity of L2 is half that of L1, find X.

Heat is supplied to a test tube containing 100 g of ice at its melting point. The ice melts completely in 1 min. What is the power rating of the source of heat? (Latent heat of fusion of ice = 336 J g^-1)
If a room is saturated with water vapour, the temperature of the room must be
options: below or at the dew point
questions.explanation: Air becomes saturated when it is at (or cooled below) its dew point.

questions.stem: The equation of a transverse wave travelling along a string is given by y = 0.3 sin(0.5x - 50t), where y and x are in cm and t is in seconds. Find the maximum displacement of the particles from the equilibrium position.
questions.explanation: The maximum displacement is the amplitude, the coefficient of the sine: 0.3 cm.

questions.stem: The sound from a source travelled to the bottom of the sea and the echo was heard 4 s later. If the speed of sound in sea water is 1500 m s^-1, the depth of the sea is
The fundamental frequency of vibration of a sonometer wire may be halved by
options: doubling the length of the wire
doubling the mass of the wire
reducing the absolute temperature by half
questions.explanation: f = (1/2L)sqrt(T/μ), so f ∝ 1/L; doubling L halves f (halving T or doubling mass only divides f by sqrt(2)).

questions.stem: A pipe of length 45 cm is closed at one end. Calculate the fundamental frequency of the sound wave generated in the pipe if the velocity of sound in air is 360 m s^-1. (Neglect end corrections.)
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe f = v/4L = 360/(4 x 0.45) = 200 Hz.

questions.stem: The note produced by a stretched string has a fundamental frequency of 400 Hz. If the length of the string is doubled while the tension in the string is increased by a factor of 4, the frequency is
questions.explanation: f ∝ sqrt(T)/L: the factor is sqrt(4)/2 = 1, so f stays 400 Hz.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: To produce a parallel beam of light from a concave mirror, the distance at which the lamp should be placed from the mirror is equal to
options: two times the radius of curvature
questions.explanation: Rays from a source at the principal focus are reflected parallel to the axis.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Light of frequency 6.0 x 10^14 Hz travelling in air is transmitted through glass of refractive index 1.5. Calculate the frequency of the light in the glass.
questions.explanation: Frequency does not change on refraction; only speed and wavelength change.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An object is placed directly below a glass block of thickness 3.0 cm. Calculate the lateral displacement of the object if the refractive index of the glass is 1.5.
questions.explanation: Apparent depth = 3.0/1.5 = 2.0 cm, so the object appears displaced by 3.0 - 2.0 = 1.0 cm.

questions.stem: In a projection lantern of focal length f, the object distance u is such that
questions.explanation: A projector forms a real, magnified image, which needs the object between f and 2f.

questions.stem: If the Nigerian flag (green, white, green) is viewed in pure yellow light, which of the following sets of colours would be observed on the flag?
questions.explanation: The green parts absorb yellow and appear black; the white part reflects yellow and appears yellow.

questions.stem: Which of the following has the lowest internal resistance when new?
questions.explanation: Lead-acid accumulators have very low internal resistance, so they can supply large currents.

questions.stem: When a biro pen rubbed on a dry silk cloth is moved very close to a piece of paper on a dry table, the pen is found to pick up the paper. This is because
options: both the pen and the cloth are magnetized
the pen is magnetized but the cloth is not
the pen is charged while the cloth is magnetized
both the pen and the cloth are charged
questions.explanation: Rubbing transfers electrons, leaving the pen and cloth with equal and opposite charges; the charged pen attracts the paper.

questions.stem: Two resistors, R1 = 4 ohms and R2 = 5 ohms, are connected in parallel across a potential difference. If P1 and P2 represent the power dissipated in R1 and R2 respectively, the ratio P1 : P2 is
questions.explanation: In parallel V is common, so P = V^2/R and P1 : P2 = 1/4 : 1/5 = 5 : 4.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are found in the receiver but not in the microphone of a telephone handset?
I. Diaphragm
II. Soft iron pole pieces
III. Permanent magnet
IV. Carbon blocks
questions.explanation: Both have a diaphragm; the carbon microphone has carbon granules/blocks, while the receiver has a permanent magnet with soft iron pole pieces.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: If two parallel conductors carry currents flowing in the same direction, the conductors will
options: both move in the same direction
have no effect on each other
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction attract; opposite currents repel.

questions.stem: A certain radioisotope of uranium, 235/92 U, emits four alpha particles and three beta particles. The mass number and the atomic number of the resulting element respectively are
If light with photon energy 2 eV is incident suitably on the surface of a metal with work function 3 eV, then
options: the few electrons emitted will have a maximum kinetic energy of 1 eV
the few electrons emitted will have a maximum kinetic energy of 3 eV
questions.explanation: The photon energy (2 eV) is less than the work function (3 eV), so no photoemission occurs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the dimension of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = MLT^-2/L^2 = ML^-1T^-2.

questions.stem: The length of a displaced pendulum bob which passes its lowest point twice every second is [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: Passing the lowest point twice per second means T = 1 s; l = gT^2/4π^2 = 10/39.5 ≈ 0.25 m.

questions.stem: When a ball rolls on a smooth level ground, the motion of its centre is
questions.explanation: The ball rotates about its centre, but the centre itself moves in a straight line: translational motion.

questions.stem: What is the acceleration due to gravity 'g' on the moon, if g is 10 m s^-2 on the earth?
questions.explanation: g on the moon is about one-sixth of that on earth: 10/6 ≈ 1.67 m s^-2.

questions.stem: A body is projected from the earth's surface with the intention of letting it escape from the earth's gravitational field. What is the minimum escape velocity of the body?
questions.explanation: The earth's escape velocity sqrt(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km s^-1.

questions.stem: A uniform rod PQ of length 1 m and mass 2 kg is pivoted at the end P. If a load of 14 N is placed at the centre of the rod, find the force that should be applied vertically upwards at Q to maintain the rod in equilibrium horizontally. [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: Moments about P: F x 1 = (20 + 14) x 0.5, so F = 17 N.

questions.stem: A vehicle of mass m is driven by an engine of power P from rest. Find the minimum time it will take to acquire a speed v.
questions.explanation: Work done Pt = kinetic energy ½mv^2, so t = mv^2/(2P).

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: The energy contained in a wire when it is extended by 0.02 m by a force of 500 N is
A hydraulic press has a large circular piston of radius 0.8 m and a circular plunger of radius 0.2 m. A force of 500 N is exerted by the plunger. Find the force exerted on the piston.
questions.explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally: F = 500 x (0.8/0.2)^2 = 8000 N.

questions.stem: The volume of an air bubble increases from the bottom to the top of a lake at constant temperature because
options: atmospheric pressure acts on the surface of the lake
pressure increases with depth of the lake
questions.explanation: Pressure is greater at depth; as the bubble rises the pressure falls, so by Boyle's law its volume increases.

questions.stem: Temperature is a measure of the
options: quantity of heat transferred into the molecules of an object
mean kinetic energy of the molecules of the object
kinetic energy of any individual molecule of the substance
amount of work done by the molecules of the object
questions.explanation: By kinetic theory, temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules.

questions.stem: A piece of wood floats in water at room temperature with a fraction of it above the liquid surface. As the temperature of the water is raised, the part of the wood above the liquid surface will
options: decrease because the density of water decreases with temperature
increase because the density of water decreases with temperature
decrease because the density of water increases with temperature
increase because the density of water increases with temperature
questions.explanation: Warmer water is less dense, so a larger volume must be displaced to support the wood and less of it shows above the surface.

questions.stem: The equation P^x V^y T^z = constant is Charles' law when
questions.explanation: Charles' law (pressure constant) is V/T = constant, i.e. x = 0, y = 1, z = -1.

questions.stem: An electric kettle with negligible heat capacity is rated at 2000 W. If 2.0 kg of water is put in it, how long will it take the temperature of the water to rise from 20 °C to 100 °C? [specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1]
A temperature scale has a lower fixed point of 40 mm and an upper fixed point of 200 mm. What is the reading on this scale when a thermometer reads 60 °C?
A quantity of ice at -10 °C is heated until the temperature of the heating vessel is 90 °C. Which of the following constants is NOT required in the calculation of the heat supplied?
questions.explanation: The water never reaches 100 °C, so no vaporization occurs and its latent heat is not needed.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements give the TRUE differences between evaporation and boiling?
I. Evaporation occurs at all temperatures while boiling occurs at a fixed temperature for a given pressure.
II. Evaporation is a surface phenomenon while boiling is an interior phenomenon.
III. Evaporation is affected by surface area while boiling is not.
questions.explanation: All three are standard differences between evaporation and boiling.

questions.stem: A well-lagged bar of length 100 cm has its ends maintained at 100 °C and 40 °C respectively. What is the temperature at a point 60 cm from the hotter end?
questions.explanation: In a lagged bar the temperature falls uniformly: 100 - (60/100)(60) = 64 °C.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the exclusive property of a transverse wave?
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarized.

questions.stem: The wavelength of the signal from a radio transmitter is 1500 m and the frequency is 200 kHz. What is the wavelength for a transmitter operating at 1000 kHz?
questions.explanation: v = fλ is constant: λ = 1500 x 200/1000 = 300 m.

questions.stem: The difference between sound waves and light waves is that sound waves
options: are transverse while light waves are longitudinal
require a medium to travel while light waves do not
can be diffracted but light waves cannot
cannot be reflected but light waves can
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave needing a material medium; light is electromagnetic and travels through a vacuum.

questions.stem: The pitch of an acoustic device can be increased by
questions.explanation: Pitch depends on frequency; amplitude and intensity affect loudness.

questions.stem: A total eclipse of the sun occurs when the
options: earth is between the moon and the sun
sun is between the moon and the earth
moon is between the sun and the earth
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the moon comes between the sun and the earth and casts its shadow on the earth.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: What is the approximate critical angle for total internal reflection for diamond if the refractive index of diamond is 2.42?

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A real object is placed at a distance u cm in front of a curved mirror of focal length f cm. If the image is upright and magnified, then the mirror is
questions.explanation: Only a concave mirror with the object inside f gives an upright magnified image; u = f/2 gives v = -f, a virtual image twice the size.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of colours gives the widest separation in the spectrum of white light?
questions.explanation: Red and violet are at opposite ends of the visible spectrum.

questions.stem: Two parallel plates at a distance of 8.0 x 10^-3 m apart are maintained at a p.d. of 600 volts with the negative plate earthed. What is the electric field strength?
At different locations on the earth's surface, the earth's magnetic field is
options: the same in magnitude and direction
the same in magnitude but different in direction
different in both magnitude and direction
different in magnitude but not in direction
questions.explanation: Both the strength and the direction (dip and declination) of the earth's field vary from place to place.

questions.stem: If a resistance is halved in value and the potential difference across it is tripled, then the ratio of the new current to the old is
questions.explanation: I = V/R, so the new current is 3/(1/2) = 6 times the old: 6 : 1.

questions.stem: A 12-V battery has an internal resistance of 0.5 ohms. If a cable of 1.0 ohm resistance is connected across the two terminals of the battery, the current drawn from the battery is
The purpose of a dielectric material in a parallel plate capacitor is to
options: insulate the plates from each other
increase the magnetic field between the plates
questions.explanation: C = εA/d; a dielectric raises the permittivity and so increases the capacitance.

questions.stem: An electric current of 2 amperes flows in a heating coil of resistance 50 ohms for 3 minutes 20 seconds. Determine the heat produced.
If the maximum voltage across a 100-ohm resistor is 20 V, then the maximum power it can dissipate is
Which of the following is required to convert a milliammeter to an ammeter?
questions.explanation: A low-resistance shunt in parallel carries most of the current.

questions.stem: The primary winding of a transformer has 400 turns and its secondary has 100 turns. If a source of e.m.f. of 12 V is applied to the primary, the secondary e.m.f. will be
questions.explanation: Vs = Vp x Ns/Np = 12 x 100/400 = 3 V.

questions.stem: An alternating source is connected in series to a capacitor of capacitive reactance 1000 sqrt(3) ohms and a resistor of resistance 10^3 ohms. The impedance of the circuit is
The half-life of a radioactive element is 9 days. What fraction of atoms has decayed in 36 days?
questions.explanation: 36 days = 4 half-lives; remaining = 1/16, so 15/16 has decayed.

questions.stem: Light of energy 5 eV falls on a metal and electrons with a maximum kinetic energy of 2 eV are ejected. The work function of the metal is
questions.explanation: W = hf - KEmax = 5 - 2 = 3.0 eV.

questions.stem: The distance x m travelled by a particle in time t seconds is described by the equation x = 10 + 12t^2. Find the average speed of the particle between the time interval t = 2 s and t = 5 s.
questions.explanation: x(5) = 310 m and x(2) = 58 m; average speed = 252/3 = 84 m s^-1.

questions.stem: A 5 kg block is released from rest on a smooth plane inclined at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. What is its acceleration down the plane? [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: On a smooth incline a = g sin θ = 10 x 0.5 = 5.0 m s^-2.

questions.stem: An arrow of mass 0.1 kg moving with a horizontal velocity of 15 m s^-1 is shot into a wooden block of mass 0.4 kg lying at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. Their common velocity after impact is
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 0.1 x 15 = 0.5v, so v = 3.0 m s^-1.

questions.stem: Two bodies X and Y are projected on the same horizontal plane with the same initial speed but at angles of 30° and 60° respectively to the horizontal. Neglecting air resistance, the ratio of the range of X to that of Y is
questions.explanation: R = u^2 sin 2θ/g and sin 60° = sin 120°, so the ranges are equal.

questions.stem: Which of the following, with respect to a body performing simple harmonic motion, are in phase?
options: Displacement and velocity of the body
Displacement and force on the body
Velocity and acceleration of the body
Force acting on the body and the acceleration
questions.explanation: F = ma, so force and acceleration always point the same way; displacement and force are in antiphase.

questions.stem: A body of mass 2 kg moving vertically upwards has its velocity increased uniformly from 10 m s^-1 to 40 m s^-1 in 4 s. Neglecting air resistance, calculate the upward vertical force acting on the body. [g = 10 m s^-2]

A planet has mass m1 and is at a distance r1 from the sun. A second planet has mass m2 = 10m1 and is at a distance r2 = 2r1 from the sun. Determine the ratio of the gravitational forces experienced by the planets.
A block of mass m slides down a rough inclined plane QP at an angle θ. The forces acting on the block along the plane QP are
options: mg sin θ and the normal reaction
mg sin θ and the force of friction
mg cos θ and the normal reaction
mg cos θ and the force of friction
questions.explanation: Along the plane act the weight component mg sin θ and friction; mg cos θ and the normal reaction are perpendicular to it.

questions.stem: An object of mass 100 g projected vertically upwards from the ground level has a velocity of 20 m s^-1 at a height of 10 m. Calculate its initial kinetic energy at the ground level. [g = 10 m s^-2; neglect air resistance]
An electric water pump rated 1.5 kW lifts 200 kg of water through a vertical height of 6 metres in 10 seconds. What is the efficiency of the pump? [g = 10 m s^-2; neglect air resistance]
questions.explanation: Useful power = 200 x 10 x 6/10 = 1200 W; efficiency = 1200/1500 = 80%.

questions.stem: For a rough inclined plane on which lies a body of weight W, the angle of inclination θ of the plane becomes the angle of friction if
options: tan θ = coefficient of static friction
cos θ = coefficient of dynamic friction
sin θ = coefficient of sliding friction
questions.explanation: At the angle of friction the body is just about to slide: mg sin θ = μ mg cos θ, so tan θ = μ (static).

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A load of 20 N on a wire of cross-sectional area 8 x 10^-7 m^2 produces an extension of 10^-4 m. Calculate Young's modulus for the material of the wire if its length is 3 m.
A cube of sides 0.1 m hangs freely from a string. What is the upthrust on the cube when totally immersed in water? [Density of water is 1000 kg m^-3, g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: Upthrust = Vρg = 0.001 x 1000 x 10 = 10 N.

questions.stem: A piece of wire gauze can be made to lie on water because
options: the wire gauze is less dense than water
the water molecules repel the wire gauze upwards
the water surface has the effect of an elastic thin skin
of the cohesive forces between the water and the wire gauze molecules
questions.explanation: Surface tension makes the water surface behave like a stretched elastic skin that supports the gauze.

questions.stem: A liquid of mass 1.0 x 10^3 kg fills a rectangular tank of length 2.5 m and width 2.0 m. If the tank is 4 m high, what is the pressure at the middle of the tank? [g = 10 m s^-2]
An empty 60 litre petrol tank has a mass of 10 kg. Its mass when full of fuel of relative density 0.72 is
questions.explanation: Mass of fuel = 60 L x 0.72 kg/L = 43.2 kg; total = 43.2 + 10 = 53.2 kg.

questions.stem: The length of a mercury thread when it is at 0 °C, 100 °C and at an unknown temperature θ is 25 mm, 225 mm and 174 mm respectively. The value of θ is
questions.explanation: θ = (174 - 25)/(225 - 25) x 100 = 74.5 °C, which is approximately 75 °C.

questions.stem: Equal masses of copper and rubber are raised to the same temperature. After some time, the copper was observed to be at a lower temperature because
options: the specific heat capacity of copper is lower than that of rubber
the specific heat capacity of rubber is lower than that of copper
questions.explanation: Copper has the lower specific heat capacity, so losing the same heat makes its temperature fall more.

questions.stem: Before starting a journey, the tyre pressure of a car was 3 x 10^5 N m^-2 at 27 °C. At the end of the journey, the pressure rose to 4 x 10^5 N m^-2. Calculate the temperature of the tyre after the journey, assuming the volume is constant.
A heating coil rated at 1000 W is used to boil off 0.5 kg of boiling water. The time taken to boil off the water is [Specific latent heat of vaporization of water = 2.3 x 10^6 J kg^-1]
What happens when a certain quantity of pure ice is completely changed to water at 0 °C?
options: Latent heat is absorbed, the mass remains constant and the volume decreases
Latent heat is given out, the mass remains constant and the volume decreases
Latent heat is given out, the mass increases and the volume remains constant
Latent heat is absorbed, the mass decreases and the volume increases
questions.explanation: Melting absorbs latent heat; mass is unchanged and, since ice is less dense than water, the volume decreases.

questions.stem: Ripples on water and light waves are similar because both
questions.explanation: Both are transverse waves showing reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference.

questions.stem: Under constant tension and constant mass per unit length, the note produced by a plucked string is 500 Hz when the length of the string is 0.90 m. At what length is the frequency 150 Hz?
The colours seen in thin films of oil on the road and in soap bubbles are due to
questions.explanation: Light reflected from the top and bottom of the thin film interferes, reinforcing different colours at different thicknesses.

questions.stem: If the load at the end of a sonometer wire is immersed in a bucket of water, the original fundamental frequency of the wire could be restored by
options: decreasing the length of the wire
increasing the length of the wire
increasing the mass per unit length of the wire
changing the temperature of the water
questions.explanation: Upthrust reduces the tension and so lowers f = (1/2L)sqrt(T/μ); shortening the wire raises f back.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A boy, on looking into a mirror, observed that his face appeared to have grown bigger. The boy must have been looking at a
options: convex mirror with his face at the focus
concave mirror with his face between the focus and the mirror
concave mirror with his face at the focus
convex mirror with his face between the focus and the mirror
questions.explanation: A concave mirror gives an erect magnified virtual image when the object is between F and the pole; a convex mirror always diminishes.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Light of velocity 3.0 x 10^8 m s^-1 is incident on a material of refractive index n. If the velocity of light is reduced to 2.4 x 10^8 m s^-1 in the material, what is n?
A patient with a sight defect has a distance of distinct vision of 150 cm. For him to be able to read a material placed at a distance of 25 cm, what is the focal length of the glasses he should wear?
questions.explanation: The lens must form a virtual image at 150 cm of an object at 25 cm: 1/f = 1/25 - 1/150, so f = 30 cm (converging).

questions.stem: The electromagnetic waves that are sensitive to temperature changes are
questions.explanation: Infra-red radiation is heat radiation and is detected by its heating effect.

questions.stem: A galvanometer of internal resistance 50 ohms has a full scale deflection for a current of 5 mA. What is the resistance required to convert it to a voltmeter with full scale deflection of 10 V?
questions.explanation: R = V/I - r = 10/0.005 - 50 = 1950 Ω, connected in series.

questions.stem: If 8 x 10^-2 J of work is required to move 100 μC of charge from a point X to a point Y in an electrical circuit, the potential difference between X and Y is
In a metre bridge experiment, two resistors 2 ohms and 3 ohms occupy the left and right gaps respectively. Find the balance point from the left side of the bridge.
Two 50 μF parallel plate capacitors are connected in series. The combined capacitor is then connected across a 100-V battery. The charge on each plate of the capacitor is
questions.explanation: Series combination = 25 μF; Q = CV = 25 x 10^-6 x 100 = 2.5 x 10^-3 C.

questions.stem: What is the total electrical energy consumed by using an electric cooker rated 1000 W for 5 hrs?
The power dissipated in an a.c. circuit with an r.m.s. current of 5 A, r.m.s. voltage of 10 V and a phase angle of 60° is
questions.explanation: P = IV cos φ = 5 x 10 x 0.5 = 25 W.

questions.stem: The voltage of the domestic electric supply is represented by the equation V = 311 sin 314.2t. Determine the frequency of the a.c. supply. [π = 3.142]
In a purely inductive circuit, the current
options: lags behind the voltage in phase by 90°
leads the voltage in phase by 90°
is in the same phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a pure inductor the current lags the voltage by 90°.

questions.stem: One of the features of the fission process is that
options: the sum of the masses of the reactants equals the sum of the masses of the products
questions.explanation: Each fission releases neutrons that can split further nuclei, giving a chain reaction.

questions.stem: The graphite rods surrounding the uranium fuel rods in a nuclear reactor are used to
options: absorb the neutrons and hence halt the nuclear process
create the neutrons and hence start up the nuclear process
slow down the neutrons and hence slow the nuclear process
speed up the neutrons and hence speed up the nuclear process
questions.explanation: Graphite is a moderator: it slows down fast neutrons. C is the only option describing that role (control rods, not graphite, absorb neutrons).

questions.stem: The physical quantity that has the same dimensions as impulse is
questions.explanation: Impulse = force x time = change in momentum, so both have dimensions MLT^-1.

questions.stem: In free fall, a body of mass 1kg drops from a height of 125m from rest in 5s. How long will it take another body of mass 2kg to fall from rest from the same height? (g = 10 m s^-2)
questions.explanation: In free fall the acceleration g is independent of mass, so the 2 kg body also takes 5 s (h = ½gt^2 gives t = 5 s).

questions.stem: A ball of mass 0.15kg is kicked against a rigid vertical wall with a horizontal velocity of 50 m s^-1, calculate the impulse of the ball on the wall.
questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum = mv = 0.15 x 50 = 7.5 Ns (ball brought to rest by the wall).

questions.stem: The force of attraction between two point masses is 10^-4 N when the distance between them is 0.18m. If the distance is reduced to 0.06m, calculate the force.
questions.explanation: F is proportional to 1/r^2; the distance is divided by 3 so the force is multiplied by 9: 9.0 x 10^-4 N.

questions.stem: A uniform metre rule weighing 0.5N is to be pivoted on a knife-edge at the 30cm-mark. Where will a force of 2N be placed from the pivot to balance the metre rule?
questions.explanation: The weight acts at the 50 cm mark, 20 cm from the pivot: 0.5 x 20 = 2 x d, so d = 5 cm.

questions.stem: A bullet fired at a wooden block of thickness 0.15m manages to penetrate the block. If the mass of the bullet is 0.025kg and the average resisting force of the wood is 7.5 x 10^3 N, calculate the speed of the bullet just before it hits the wooden block.
A man whose mass is 80kg climbs a staircase in 20s and expends a power of 120W. Find the height of the staircase. [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: Pt = mgh: 120 x 20 = 80 x 10 x h, so h = 3.0 m.

questions.stem: A parachute attains a terminal velocity when
options: Its density is equal to the density of air
The viscous force of the air and the upthrust completely counteract its weight
It expands as a result of reduced external pressure
The viscous force of the air is equal to the sum of the weight and upthrust
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the net force is zero: viscous drag + upthrust = weight.

questions.stem: In a wheel and axle mechanism, the diameters of the wheel and axle are 40cm and 8cm respectively. Given that the machine is 80% efficient, what effort is required to lift a load of 100N?

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: The tendon in a man's leg is 0.01m long. If a force of 5N stretches the tendon by 2.0 x 10^-5 m, calculate the strain on the muscle.
questions.explanation: Strain = extension/length = 2.0 x 10^-5 / 0.01 = 2 x 10^-3.

questions.stem: Which of these statements are correct for the pressures in liquids? I. Pressure in a liquid at a point acts equally in all directions. II. Pressure increases with depth. III. Pressure at a depth depends on the shape of the container. IV. Pressures at the same depth in different liquids are proportional to the densities of the liquids.
questions.explanation: p = hρg acts equally in all directions and does not depend on the shape of the container, so III is false.

questions.stem: The atmospheric pressure due to water is 1.3 x 10^6 N m^-2. What is the total pressure at the bottom of an ocean 10m deep?
A solid of weight 0.600N is totally immersed in oil and water respectively. If the upthrust in oil is 0.210N and the relative density of oil is 0.875 find the upthrust in water.
questions.explanation: Relative density = upthrust in oil / upthrust in water, so upthrust in water = 0.210/0.875 = 0.240 N.

questions.stem: A platinum resistance thermometer records 3.0 Ω at 0°C and 8.0 Ω at 100°C. If it records 6.0 Ω in a certain environment, the temperature of the medium is
The linear expansivity of brass is 2 x 10^-5 °C^-1. If the volume of a piece of brass is 15.00 cm^3 at 0°C, what is the volume at 100°C?
questions.explanation: Cubic expansivity = 3 x 2 x 10^-5 = 6 x 10^-5; ΔV = 15 x 6 x 10^-5 x 100 = 0.09 cm^3, so V = 15.09 cm^3.

questions.stem: A gas has a volume of 100 cm^3 at 27°C. If it is heated to temperature T until a final volume of 120 cm^3 is attained, calculate T.
questions.explanation: Charles's law: T = 300 x 120/100 = 360 K = 87°C.

questions.stem: A 500W heater is used to heat 0.6kg of water from 25°C to 100°C in t1 seconds. If another 1000W heater is used to heat 0.2kg of water from 10°C to 100°C in t2 seconds, find t1/t2.

How many grams of water at 17°C must be added to 42g of ice at 0°C to melt the ice completely? [Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.4 x 10^5 J kg^-1, Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1]
questions.explanation: Heat to melt ice = 0.042 x 3.4 x 10^5 = 14280 J = m x 4200 x 17, so m = 0.2 kg = 200 g.

questions.stem: A vapour is said to be saturated when
options: More molecules return to the liquid than the amount that left it
A dynamic equilibrium exists between the molecules of the liquid and the vapour molecules at a given temperature
The vapour pressure is equal to the atmospheric pressure
All molecules are moving with the same speed in all directions at a given temperature
questions.explanation: A saturated vapour is in dynamic equilibrium with its liquid: molecules leave and return at equal rates.

questions.stem: One valid assumption of the kinetic theory of gases is that
options: The molecules of a gas are constantly in a state of motion and the number of collisions remain constant
The number of molecules of gas increases with increasing pressure
As the temperature increases, the number of collisions made by the gas molecules remain constant
The molecules of gas are all identical and are very small in size
questions.explanation: The kinetic theory assumes identical molecules of negligible size; collision rates change with conditions, so A and C are not assumptions.

questions.stem: The physical properties of sound waves can best be described by
questions.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal wave, so it cannot be polarized; it shows reflection and diffraction.

questions.stem: The velocity of a sound wave at 27°C is 360 m s^-1. Its velocity at 127°C is
questions.explanation: v is proportional to sqrt(T): v = 360 x sqrt(400/300) = 720/√3 = 240√3 m/s.

questions.stem: In a closed organ pipe producing a musical note, an antinode will always be produced at
options: All the parts of the pipe
questions.explanation: In a closed pipe the closed end is always a displacement node and the open end is always an antinode.

questions.stem: A steel wire of length 0.50m is stretched between two fixed points and its fundamental frequency is 200Hz. The speed of the wave in the wire is
questions.explanation: Fundamental: λ = 2L = 1.0 m, so v = fλ = 200 x 1.0 = 200 m/s.

questions.stem: In a resonance tube experiment, if the fundamental frequency of the vibrating air column is 280Hz, the frequency of the third overtone is
questions.explanation: A resonance tube is closed at one end, so only odd harmonics occur: the third overtone is the 7th harmonic = 7 x 280 = 1960 Hz.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An object O lies at a distance m in front of a concave mirror of focal length f. If m < f, then the final image obtained will be
questions.explanation: An object inside the focal length of a concave mirror gives a virtual, erect, magnified image.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An object is placed in front of two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ°. If the total number of images formed is 7, find the value of θ.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The most suitable type of mirror used for the construction of a searchlight is the
questions.explanation: A parabolic mirror sends light from a source at its focus out as a parallel beam without spherical aberration.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The displacement d produced in a glass block of thickness t and refractive index n when an object is viewed through it is
questions.explanation: Apparent depth = t/n, so the displacement = t - t/n = t(1 - 1/n).

questions.stem: A man wears convex lens glasses of focal length 30cm in order to correct his eye defect. Instead of the optimum 25cm, his least distance of distinct vision is
questions.explanation: The lens forms a virtual image of an object at 25 cm at his near point: 1/v = 1/30 - 1/25 = -1/150, so the near point is 150 cm.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true about infra-red radiation? I. It is invisible. II. It is called heat ray. III. Its frequency is higher than that of blue light. IV. It travels as a transverse wave.
questions.explanation: Infra-red has a lower frequency than visible (blue) light, so III is false; the rest are true.

questions.stem: The force of repulsion between two point positive charges 5 μC and 8 μC separated at a distance of 0.02m apart is
An ebonite rod rubbed with fur attracts a glass rod rubbed with silk because
options: Ebonite has a negative charge while glass has a positive charge
Ebonite has a positive charge while glass has a negative charge
questions.explanation: Ebonite rubbed with fur becomes negative and glass rubbed with silk becomes positive; unlike charges attract.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to reduce local action in a Leclanche cell?
options: A carbon rod as the positive pole
Pure zinc as the negative pole
Potassium permanganate solution in contact with the positive pole
questions.explanation: Local action is caused by impurities in the zinc; using pure (or amalgamated) zinc reduces it.

questions.stem: Find the work done in moving a 2C charge between two points X and Y in an electric field if the potential difference is 100 volts.
A parallel plate capacitor has a common plate area of 5 x 10^-8 m^2 and plate separation of 2 x 10^-3 m. Assuming free space, what is the capacitance?
questions.explanation: C = ε0A/d = 9 x 10^-12 x 5 x 10^-8 / 2 x 10^-3 = 2.25 x 10^-16 F (taking ε0 ≈ 9 x 10^-12 F/m; the exponent signs were lost in the source text and are restored here).
