questions.stem: The iron core of an induction coil is made from bundles of wires so as to
options: Prevent sparking at the contact breaker
Get the greatest possible secondary voltage
questions.explanation: Splitting the core into insulated wires breaks up eddy-current paths and reduces energy loss.

questions.stem: Electricity is supplied to a school along a cable of total resistance 0.5 Ω with the maximum current drawn from the mains as 100A. The maximum energy dissipated as heat for 1hr is
A transformer which can produce 8V from a 240V a.c. supply, has an efficiency of 80%. If the current in the secondary coil is 15A, calculate the current in the primary coil.
questions.explanation: Output = 8 x 15 = 120 W; input = 120/0.8 = 150 W; primary current = 150/240 = 0.625 A.

questions.stem: The electrochemical equivalent of a metal is 1.3 x 10^-7 kg C^-1. The mass of the metal which 2.0 x 10^4 C of electricity will deposit from a suitable electrolyte is
A radioactive substance has a half-life of 80 days. If the initial number of atoms in the sample is 6.0 x 10^10, how many atoms would remain at the end of 320 days?
In a nuclear fusion experiment, the loss of mass amounts to 1.0 x 10^-6 kg. The amount of energy obtained from the fusion is [Speed of light = 3.0 x 10^8 m s^-1]
In photoelectric effect, electrons will leave the metal surface when illuminated by light of appropriate frequency if the photon energy is
options: Equal to the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons
questions.explanation: Photoemission with kinetic energy occurs when hf exceeds the work function (hf = W + ½mv^2).

questions.stem: A car of mass 800kg attains a speed of 25 m s^-1 in 20 seconds. The power developed in the engine is
A lead bullet of mass 0.05kg is fired with a velocity of 200 m s^-1 into a lead block of mass 0.95 kg. Given that the lead block can move freely, the final kinetic energy after impact is
questions.explanation: Momentum: 0.05 x 200 = 1.0 x v, so v = 10 m/s; KE = ½ x 1.0 x 10^2 = 50 J.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 0.1kg is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 10 m s^-1 from the top of a tower 10m high. Neglecting air resistance, its total energy just before hitting the ground is [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: Total energy is conserved: ½ x 0.1 x 10^2 + 0.1 x 10 x 10 = 5 + 10 = 15 J.

questions.stem: A solid figure with base PQ and centre of gravity G rests on an inclined plane. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The solid will fall over if the vertical line through G lies outside the base
The solid will fall over if the vertical line through G lies inside the base
The solid will not fall over if the vertical line through G lies outside the base
The solid can never fall over
questions.explanation: A body topples when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base.

questions.stem: Two bodies have masses in the ratio 3 : 1. They experience forces which impart to them accelerations in the ratio 2 : 9 respectively. Find the ratio of the forces the masses experience.
A particle of mass 10^-2 kg is fixed to the tip of a fan blade which rotates with angular velocity of 100 rad s^-1. If the radius of the blade is 0.2m, the centripetal force is
The inner diameter of a small test tube can be measured accurately using a
questions.explanation: Vernier calipers have inside jaws for internal diameters; a micrometer cannot measure an inner diameter.

questions.stem: A gas at a volume V0 in a container at pressure P0, is compressed to one fifth of its volume. What will be its pressure if it maintains its original temperature T?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: PV is constant, so a fifth of the volume gives 5P0.

questions.stem: A piece of substance of specific heat capacity 450 J kg^-1 K^-1 falls through a vertical distance of 20m from rest. Calculate the rise in temperature of the substance on hitting the ground when all its energies are converted into heat. [g = 10 m s^-2]
questions.explanation: mgh = mcΔθ: Δθ = gh/c = 10 x 20 / 450 = 4/9 °C.

questions.stem: In a J-tube, Y and X are on the same horizontal level and 30 cm^3 of air is trapped above Y when the atmospheric pressure is 75 cmHg. Calculate the volume of air trapped above Y when 15 cmHg is now poured into the limb above X.
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: 75 x 30 = (75 + 15) x V, so V = 25 cm^3.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: If the stress on a wire is 10^7 N m^-2 and the wire is stretched from its original length of 10.00cm to 10.05 cm, the Young's modulus of the wire is
A solid weighs 10.0N in air, 6.0 N when fully immersed in water and 7.0 N when fully immersed in a certain liquid X. Calculate the relative density of the liquid.
questions.explanation: RD = upthrust in liquid / upthrust in water = (10 - 7)/(10 - 6) = 3/4.

questions.stem: I. A liquid boils when its saturated vapour pressure is equal to the external pressure. II. Dissolved substances in pure water lead to increase in the boiling point. III. When the external pressure is increased, the boiling point increases. IV. Dissolved substances in pure water decrease the boiling point. Which combination of the above are peculiarities of the boiling point of a liquid?
questions.explanation: Dissolved impurities raise (not lower) the boiling point, so IV is false; I, II and III are true.

questions.stem: When the temperature of a liquid is increased, its surface tension
questions.explanation: Surface tension decreases as temperature rises because intermolecular attraction weakens.

questions.stem: When the brakes in a car are applied, the frictional force on the tyres is
options: A disadvantage because it is in the direction of motion of the car
A disadvantage because it is in the opposite direction of motion of the car
An advantage because it is in the direction of motion of the car
An advantage because it is in the opposite direction of motion of the car
questions.explanation: Braking friction opposes the motion and so helps to stop the car: an advantage.

questions.stem: The lowest note emitted by a stretched string has a frequency of 40Hz. How many overtones are there between 40Hz and 180Hz?
questions.explanation: A string gives all harmonics: 80, 120 and 160 Hz lie between 40 and 180 Hz, i.e. 3 overtones. (The source text reads "400Hz", an extraction error for 40 Hz.)

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A man stands 4m in front of a plane mirror. If the mirror is moved 1m towards the man, the distance between him and his image is
questions.explanation: He is now 3 m from the mirror and his image is 3 m behind it: 6 m apart.

questions.stem: If a sound wave goes from a cold-air region to a hot-air region, its wavelength
questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in hot air while frequency is unchanged, so λ = v/f increases.

questions.stem: The equation of a wave traveling along the positive x-direction is given by y = 0.25 x 10^-3 sin(500t - 0.025x). Determine the angular frequency of the wave motion.
questions.explanation: Comparing with y = A sin(ωt - kx), ω = 500 rad/s = 5.00 x 10^2 rad s^-1.

questions.stem: Calculate the mass of ice that would melt when 2kg of copper is quickly transferred from boiling water to a block of ice without heat loss. [Specific heat capacity of copper = 400 J kg^-1 K^-1; Latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.3 x 10^5 J kg^-1]
questions.explanation: Heat from copper cooling 100°C to 0°C = 2 x 400 x 100 = 80000 J; mass melted = 80000/330000 = 8/33 kg.

questions.stem: The temperature gradient across a copper rod of thickness 0.02m, maintained at two temperature junctions of 20°C and 80°C respectively is
Four cells each of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance of 4 Ohms are connected in parallel. What is the effective e.m.f. and internal resistance of the combination?
questions.explanation: Identical cells in parallel keep the e.m.f. of one cell (1.5 V); internal resistance = 4/4 = 1 Ω.

questions.stem: An astronomical telescope is said to be in normal adjustment when the
options: Focal length of objective lens is longer than that of eye piece
Final image is at the near point of eye
questions.explanation: In normal adjustment the final image is formed at infinity (the eye is relaxed).

questions.stem: Steel is more suitable for permanent magnets than iron because the former
options: Is easily demagnetized by shaking vigorously
Is an alloy of many metals
Is easily magnetized by alternating current through one cycle
questions.explanation: Steel has high retentivity (coercivity), so it keeps its magnetism.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The velocities of light in air and glass are 3.0 x 10^8 m s^-1 and 2.0 x 10^8 m s^-1 respectively. If the angle of refraction is 30°, the sine of the angle of incidence is
The core of an efficient transformer should consist of laminated pieces of metal in order to
options: Increase the heat produced by increasing the eddy current
Increase the heat produced by reducing the eddy current
Reduce the heat produced by increasing the eddy current
Reduce the heat produced by reducing the eddy current
questions.explanation: Lamination reduces eddy currents and hence the heat wasted in the core.

questions.stem: In Fleming's right-hand rule, the thumb, the forefinger and the middle finger if held mutually at right angles represent respectively, the
options: Motion, the field and induced current
Induced current, the motion and the field
Field, the induced current and the motion
Induced current, the field and the motion
questions.explanation: Right-hand (dynamo) rule: thuMb = Motion, First finger = Field, seCond finger = induced Current.

questions.stem: At what frequency would a 10 H inductor have a reactance of 2000 ohms?
A 3000 W electric cooker is to be used on a 200V mains circuit. Which of the fuses below can be used safely with the cooker?
questions.explanation: I = P/V = 3000/200 = 15 A, so the fuse must be rated above 15 A: 20 A.

questions.stem: A galvanometer has a resistance of 5 Ω. By using a shunt wire of resistance 0.05 Ω, the galvanometer could be converted to an ammeter capable of reading 2 A. What is the current through the galvanometer?

If Δx is the uncertainty in the measurement of the position of a particle along the x-axis and ΔPx is the uncertainty in the measurement of the linear momentum along the x-axis, then the uncertainty principle relation is given as
questions.explanation: Heisenberg's principle: the product of the uncertainties cannot be less than about h (Δx ΔPx ≥ h).

questions.stem: 23/11 Na + proton → q/p X + alpha particle. What are the values of p and q respectively in the equation above? (Na: mass number 23, atomic number 11)
questions.explanation: Atomic numbers: 11 + 1 = p + 2, so p = 10; mass numbers: 23 + 1 = q + 4, so q = 20.

questions.stem: A semi-conductor diode is used in rectifying alternating current into direct current mainly because it
options: Allows current to flow in either direction
Allows current to flow only in one direction
questions.explanation: A diode conducts in one direction only, which converts a.c. to d.c.

questions.stem: In semi-conductors, the carriers of current at room temperature are
questions.explanation: Conduction in semiconductors is by both electrons and holes.

questions.stem: What is the speed of a particle of mass 10^-27 kg whose wavelength is 10^-8 m? (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 Js)
In a series R-L-C circuit at resonance, the voltages across the resistor and the inductor are 30 V and 40 V respectively. What is the voltage across the capacitor?
questions.explanation: At resonance XL = XC, so VC = VL = 40 V.

questions.stem: Gamma rays are produced when
options: High velocity electrons are abruptly stopped in metals
Energy changes occur within the nucleus of atoms
Energy changes occur within the electronic structure of atoms
Electrons are deflected in very strong magnetic fields
questions.explanation: Gamma rays come from energy transitions within the nucleus (A describes X-ray production).

questions.stem: In the Rutherford scattering experiment, a beam of alpha particles was fired at a thin gold film with some of the particles being considerably deflected. This shows that
options: A gold nucleus contains protons, neutrons and electrons uniformly distributed in a tiny volume
The gold nucleus is positively charged and is concentrated in a tiny volume
The gold nucleus emitted alpha particles
The gold nucleus is concentrated in a tiny volume and contains alpha particles
questions.explanation: Large deflections of positive alpha particles show a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus
questions.stem: A catapult used to hold a stone of mass 500g is extended by 20cm with an applied force F. If the stone leaves with a velocity of 40 m s^-1, the value of F is
questions.explanation: Elastic energy ½Fe = ½mv^2: ½ x F x 0.2 = ½ x 0.5 x 40^2 = 400 J, so F = 4.0 x 10^3 N.

questions.stem: A hand bag containing some load weighing 162N is carried by two students each holding the handle of the bag next to him. If each handle is pulled at 60° to the vertical, find the force on each student's arm

I. The frictional force is independent of the area of the surfaces in contact. II. The frictional force depends on the nature of the surfaces in contact. III. The frictional force depends on the speed of sliding. IV. The frictional force is directly proportional to the normal reaction. Which combination of the above is true of sliding friction?
questions.explanation: Sliding friction is independent of area and (approximately) of speed, depends on the surfaces and is proportional to the normal reaction.

questions.stem: When a ship sails from salt water into fresh water, the fraction of its volume above the water surface will
questions.explanation: Fresh water is less dense, so the ship must displace a larger volume to float; less of it is above the surface.

questions.stem: At a fixed point below a liquid surface, the pressure downward is P1 and the pressure upward is P2. It can be deduced that
questions.explanation: Pressure at a point in a fluid acts equally in all directions.

questions.stem: I. Its velocity is constant. II. No work is done on the body. III. It has constant acceleration away from the center. IV. The centripetal force is directed towards the center. Which combination of the above is true of a body moving with constant speed in a circular track?
questions.explanation: The force is always perpendicular to the motion (no work) and directed to the centre; the velocity changes direction.

questions.stem: The velocity v of a particle in a time t is given by the equation v = 10 + 2t^2. Find the instantaneous acceleration after 5 seconds.
If the force and the velocity on a system are each reduced simultaneously by half, the power of the system is
questions.explanation: P = Fv, so (½F)(½v) = ¼Fv.

questions.stem: The velocity ratio of a machine is 5 and its efficiency is 75%. What effort would be needed to lift a load of 150N with the machine?
A rope is being used to pull a mass of 10kg vertically upward. Determine the tension in the rope if, starting from rest, the mass acquires a velocity of 4 m s^-1 in 8 s.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: An engineer intends to deviate a light ray from its path 120° through reflection from a plane mirror. Calculate the angle of incidence.
questions.explanation: Deviation = 180° - 2i = 120°, so i = 30°.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: Total internal reflection occurs when light moves from
options: A dense medium to a less dense medium
A less dense medium to a dense medium
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs light going from an optically denser to a less dense medium beyond the critical angle.

questions.stem: One end of a long wire is fixed while a vibrator is attached to the other end. When the vibrator is energized, the types of waves generated in the wire are
questions.explanation: Waves reflected from the fixed end superpose with incident ones to form stationary transverse waves on the wire.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A boy observes a piece of stone at the bottom of a river 6.0m deep. If he looks from the surface of the river, what is the apparent distance of the stone from him?
questions.explanation: Apparent depth = real depth / n = 6.0/(4/3) = 4.5 m.

questions.stem: A metal of mass 0.5kg is heated to 100°C and then transferred to a well-lagged calorimeter of heat capacity 80 J K^-1 containing water of heat capacity 420 J K^-1 at 15°C. If the final steady temperature of the mixture is 25°C, find the specific heat capacity of the metal
A travelling wave moving from left to right has an amplitude of 0.15m, a frequency of 550Hz and a wavelength of 0.01m. The equation describing the wave is
A transverse wave is applied to a string whose mass per unit length is 3 x 10^-2 kg m^-1. If the string is under a tension of 12N, the speed of propagation of the wave is
questions.explanation: v = sqrt(T/μ) = sqrt(12/0.03) = 20 m/s.

questions.stem: A quantity of water at 0°C is heated to about 30°C. At each degree rise in temperature, its density will
questions.explanation: Anomalous expansion: water is densest at 4°C, so density rises from 0 to 4°C then falls.

questions.stem: A thin wire with heavy weights attached to both ends is hung over a block of ice resting on two supports. If the wire cuts through the ice block while the block remains solid behind the wire, the process is called
questions.explanation: Pressure lowers the melting point under the wire; the water refreezes above it: regelation.

questions.stem: A cell of internal resistance 0.01 ohms can be measured accurately using the
questions.explanation: A potentiometer draws no current at balance, so it measures such small internal resistances accurately.

questions.stem: An electron of charge 1.6 x 10^-19 C and mass 9.1 x 10^-31 kg is accelerated between two metal plates with a velocity of 4 x 10^7 m s^-1, the potential difference between the plates is
What optical instrument can best be constructed with converging lenses of focal lengths 500cm and 5cm?
questions.explanation: A long-focus converging objective with a short-focus converging eyepiece makes an astronomical telescope.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: If a charged ion goes through combined electric and magnetic fields, the resultant emergent velocity of the ion is
questions.explanation: Undeflected ions satisfy qE = qvB, so v = E/B.

questions.stem: A projector lantern is used to give the image of a slide on a screen. If the image is 24 times as large as the slide and the screen is 72.0m from the projecting lens, what is the position of the slide from the lens?
questions.explanation: Magnification = v/u: u = 72.0/24 = 3.0 m.

questions.stem: A radio is operated by eight cells each of e.m.f. 2.0V connected in series. If two of the cells are wrongly connected, the net e.m.f. of the radio is
questions.explanation: Each reversed cell cancels a correct one: (6 - 2) x 2.0 = 8 V.

questions.stem: A 2H inductor has negligible resistance and is connected to a 50/π Hz a.c. supply. The reactance of the inductor is
questions.explanation: XL = 2πfL = 2π x (50/π) x 2 = 200 Ω.

questions.stem: If the fraction of the atoms of a radioactive material left after 120 years is 1/64, what is the half-life of the material?
questions.explanation: 1/64 = (1/2)^6, so 6 half-lives = 120 years and the half-life = 20 years.

questions.stem: A certain radioactive source emits radiations that were found to be deflected by both magnetic and electric fields. The radiations are
questions.explanation: Only charged radiation is deflected; beta particles are electrons, while X-rays, gamma and UV are uncharged.

questions.stem: In a pure semiconductor, the number of electrons in the conduction band is
options: Equal to the number of holes in the valence band
Greater than the number of holes in the valence band
Less than the number of holes in the valence band
Twice the number of holes in the valence band
questions.explanation: In an intrinsic semiconductor each electron promoted to the conduction band leaves one hole.

questions.stem: A cell of internal resistance 1 ohm supplies current to an external resistor of 3 ohms. The efficiency of the cell is
questions.explanation: Efficiency = R/(R + r) = 3/4 = 75%.

questions.stem: Light energy 5eV falls on a metal of work function 3 eV and electrons are liberated. The stopping potential is
questions.explanation: Maximum KE = 5 - 3 = 2 eV, so the stopping potential is 2.0 V.

questions.stem: The magnetic flux in a coil having 200 turns changes at the time rate of 0.08 Wb s^-1. The induced e.m.f. in the coil is
If the frequency of an emitted x-ray is 1.6 x 10^16 Hz, the accelerating potential is
A gas would serve as an electrical conductor under
questions.explanation: Gases conduct at reduced pressure with a high p.d. driving a discharge current; option B is the only one with reduced pressure and a strong drive.

questions.stem: An electric generator with a power output of 3.0kW at a voltage of 1.5kV distributes power along cables of total resistance 20.0 ohms. The power loss in the cable is

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: A conductor of length 2m carries a current of 0.8A while kept in a magnetic field of magnetic flux density 0.5T. The maximum force acting on it is
The height at which the atmosphere ceases to exist is about 80km. If the atmospheric pressure on the ground level is 760 mmHg, the pressure at a height of 20km above the ground level is
questions.explanation: Assuming pressure falls uniformly to zero at 80 km: p = 760 x (80 - 20)/80 = 570 mmHg.

questions.stem: A stone of mass 1 kg is dropped from a height of 10m above the ground and falls freely under gravity. Its kinetic energy 5m above the ground is then equal to
options: Its kinetic energy on the ground
questions.explanation: After falling 5 m it has lost mg x 5 of its mg x 10 potential energy, which is now kinetic energy: half the initial PE.

questions.stem: If a spherical metal bob of radius 3cm is fully immersed in a cylinder containing water and the water level rises by 1cm, what is the radius of the cylinder?
The resultant of two forces acting on an object is maximum if the angle between them is
questions.explanation: Forces in the same direction (0°) add directly to give the maximum resultant.

questions.stem: The efficiency of a machine is always less than 100% because the
options: Work output is always greater than the work input
Load lifted is always greater than the effort applied
Effort applied is always greater than the load lifted
Velocity ratio is always greater than the mechanical advantage
questions.explanation: Efficiency = MA/VR; friction makes MA less than VR, so efficiency < 100%.

questions.stem: Ice cubes are added to a glass of warm water. The glass and water are cooled by
questions.explanation: Heat passes to the ice by conduction and the cooled water circulates by convection.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 35°. If the mirror is rotated through 10°, through what angle is the reflected ray rotated?
questions.explanation: Rotating a mirror through θ rotates the reflected ray through 2θ = 20°.

questions.stem: The terrestrial telescope has one extra lens more than the astronomical telescope. The extra lens is for
questions.explanation: The extra (erecting) lens inverts the image again so that it appears upright.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: The driving mirror of a car has a radius of curvature of 1m. A vehicle behind the car is 4m from the mirror. Find the image distance behind the mirror.
questions.explanation: A driving mirror is convex with f = 0.5 m: image distance = uf/(u + f) = 4 x 0.5/4.5 = 4/9 m behind the mirror.

questions.stem: The pressure of a mass of a gas changes from 300 N m^-2 to 120 N m^-2 while the temperature drops from 127°C to -73°C. The ratio of the final volume to the initial volume is
A plane sound wave of frequency 85.5 Hz and velocity 342 m s^-1 is reflected from a vertical wall. At what distance from the wall does the wave have an antinode?
questions.explanation: λ = 342/85.5 = 4 m; the wall is a node, so the first antinode is λ/4 = 1 m away.

questions.stem: A string is fastened tightly between two walls 24cm apart. The wavelength of the second overtone is
questions.explanation: The second overtone is the 3rd harmonic: L = 3λ/2, so λ = 2 x 24/3 = 16 cm.

questions.stem: A gas with initial volume of 2 x 10^-6 m^3 is allowed to expand to six times its initial volume at constant pressure of 2 x 10^5 N m^-2. The work done is
The thermometric substance of an absolute thermometer is
questions.explanation: The absolute (constant-volume gas) thermometer uses a gas such as helium or hydrogen.

questions.stem: A cell of internal resistance r supplies current to a 6.0 Ohms resistor and its efficiency is 75%. Find the value of r
A resistance R is connected across the terminals of an electric cell of internal resistance 2 Ohms and the voltage was reduced to 3/5 of its nominal value. The value of R is
A student is at a height 4m above the ground during a thunderstorm. Given that the potential difference between the thundercloud and the ground is 10^7 V, the electric field created by the storm is
questions.explanation: E = V/d = 10^7/4 = 2.5 x 10^6 N C^-1 (as intended by the question).

questions.stem: A working electric motor takes a current of 1.5A when the p.d. across it is 250V. If its efficiency is 80%, the power output is
The cost of running five 60 W lamps and four 100W lamps for 20 hours if electrical energy costs N10.00 per kWh is
questions.explanation: Power = 300 + 400 = 700 W; energy = 0.7 x 20 = 14 kWh; cost = 14 x N10 = N140.

questions.stem: In a Daniell cell, the depolarizer, positive and negative electrodes are respectively
options: Sulphuric acid, lead oxide and lead
questions.explanation: The Daniell cell uses copper sulphate as depolarizer, copper as the positive and zinc as the negative electrode.

questions.stem: A closed square box of side 0.5m is placed in a uniform electric field E. What is the flux for the box?
questions.explanation: A uniform field enters and leaves the closed box equally (no enclosed charge), so the net flux is zero.

questions.stem: A bread toaster uses a current of 4A when plugged in a 240 volts line. It takes one minute to toast slices of bread. What is the energy consumed by the toaster?
When a piece of rectangular glass block is inserted between two parallel plate capacitor, at constant plate area and distance of separation, the capacitance of the capacitor will
questions.explanation: A dielectric increases permittivity, so C = εA/d increases.

questions.stem: What is the angle of dip at the magnetic equator?
questions.explanation: At the magnetic equator the field is horizontal, so the dip is 0°.

questions.stem: A cell can supply currents of 0.4A and 0.2A through a 4.0 Ohms and 10.0 Ohms resistors respectively. The internal resistance of the cell is
The particle emitted when 39/19 K decays to 39/19 K is
questions.explanation: Mass number and atomic number are unchanged, so the nucleus only loses energy: gamma emission.

questions.stem: I. Low pressure. II. High pressure. III. High potential difference. IV. Low potential difference. Which combination of the above is true of the conduction of electricity through gases?
questions.explanation: Gases conduct at low pressure when a high potential difference is applied.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals will provide the greatest shield against ionizing radiation?
questions.explanation: Lead is the densest of these and absorbs ionizing radiation best.

questions.stem: The primary coil of a transformer has N turns and is connected to a 120 V a.c. power line. If the secondary coil has 1,000 turns and a terminal voltage of 1,200 volts, what is the value of N?
The process of energy production in the sun is
questions.explanation: The sun's energy comes from fusion of hydrogen nuclei into helium.

questions.stem: At resonance, the phase angle in an a.c. circuit is
questions.explanation: At resonance XL = XC, so current and voltage are in phase (phase angle 0°).

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: The force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field is greatest when the
options: Conductor makes an angle of 60° with the field
Force is independent of the angle between the field and the conductor
Conductor is parallel with the field
Conductor is at right angles with the field
questions.explanation: F = BIL sin θ is greatest when θ = 90°.

questions.stem: A transistor functions mainly as a
questions.explanation: Transistors are used chiefly as switches and amplifiers.

questions.stem: Energy losses through eddy currents are reduced by using
questions.explanation: Insulated soft iron wires (laminations) break up eddy-current paths.

questions.stem: A capacitor of 20 x 10^-12 F and an inductor are joined in series. The value of the inductance that will give the circuit a resonant frequency of 200 kHz is [π^2 = 10]

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.stem: The magnetic force on a charged particle moving with velocity v is
options: Proportional to both the magnitude of the charge and the velocity
Independent of the magnitude of the charge
Proportional to the velocity v only
Proportional to the magnitude of the charge only
questions.explanation: F = qvB sin θ is proportional to both q and v.

Weight is equal to the retarding force

Undeviated and undisplaced at a lower speed
Deviated and undisplaced at a lower speed
Deviated and displaced at a lower speed

questions.explanation: Air flowing past the radiator carries heat away by convection, despite the name "radiator".

options: Between the principal focus and the pole
Between the principal focus and the centre of curvature

questions.stem: The colours seen in soap bubbles are due to
questions.explanation: Light reflected from the two surfaces of the thin film interferes, reinforcing different colours at different thicknesses.

questions.stem: The phenomenon that makes sound persist when its source has been removed is known as
questions.explanation: Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to multiple reflections after the source stops.

questions.stem: Vibrations in a stretched spring cannot be polarized because they are
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarized; vibrations along a stretched spring are longitudinal.

questions.stem:
I. Temperature
II. Density of air molecules
III. Pressure
IV. Pitch

questions.explanation: Speed of sound in air depends on temperature and density; a pressure change at constant temperature does not change it, and pitch does not.

questions.stem: Water is a poor thermometric liquid because it
questions.explanation: Water wets (sticks to) glass, making readings inaccurate; it also expands irregularly.

questions.stem: The time rate of loss of heat by a body is proportional to the
options: Difference in temperature between the body and its surrounding
Ratio of the temperature of the body to that of its surrounding
questions.explanation: Newton's law of cooling: rate of heat loss is proportional to the excess temperature over the surroundings.

questions.stem: An electric iron is rated 1 000 W, 230 V. What is the resistance of its element?
The eye controls the amount of light reaching the retina by adjusting the

questions.explanation: Normal current = 1000/250 = 4 A, so the fuse chosen must be rated slightly above this: 5 A.

questions.stem: The electromagnetic wave that can produce a heating effect on the environment is
questions.explanation: Infrared radiation is absorbed and produces heating.

The particle that is responsible for nuclear fission in a nuclear reactor is
questions.explanation: Fission in a reactor is triggered by neutrons, which also sustain the chain reaction.

questions.stem:
23/11 Na + X → 20/9 F + 4/2 He (mass number/atomic number)
What particle is X in the reaction above?
questions.explanation: Mass: 23 + A = 24 gives A = 1; charge: 11 + Z = 11 gives Z = 0, so X is a neutron.

questions.stem: A transistor is used in the amplification of signals because it
questions.explanation: A small base current controls a much larger collector current, which gives amplification.

questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field

options: It has a small number of turns of coil
There is a strong permanent magnet to give high magnetic flux
The coil has a small area
There are strong hair springs to give a large control couple
questions.explanation: Sensitivity needs many turns, large area, a strong magnet and weak hair springs, so only B is true.

questions.stem: Pure silicon can be converted to a p-type material by adding a controlled amount of
questions.explanation: Trivalent (acceptor) impurities create holes, producing p-type material.

questions.stem: From the generating station to each substation power is transmitted at a very high voltage so as to reduce
questions.explanation: High voltage means low current for the same power, so I^2R heating losses are reduced.

questions.stem: The energy associated with the photon of a radio transmission at 3 x 10^5 Hz is
The carbon-granule microphone works on the principle of change in
questions.explanation: Sound pressure compresses the carbon granules, changing their resistance and hence the current.

questions.stem: A satellite is in a parking orbit if its period is
options: More than the period of the earth
Equal to the period of the earth
The square of the period of the earth
Less than the period of the earth
questions.explanation: A parking (geostationary) orbit has the same period as the earth's rotation, 24 hours.

questions.stem: A bead travelling on a straight wire is brought to rest at 0.2 m by friction. If the mass of the bead is 0.01 kg and the coefficient of friction between the bead and the wire is 0.1, determine the work done by the friction [g = 10 m s^-2]

options: Towards the centre of the circle
questions.explanation: When the centripetal force is removed the stone continues with its instantaneous velocity, which is along the tangent.

questions.stem: A test tube of radius 1.0 cm is loaded to 8.8 g. If it is placed upright in water, find the depth to which it would sink. [g = 10 m s^-2, density of water 1 000 kg m^-3]
questions.explanation: It displaces 8.8 cm^3 of water: depth = 8.8 / (pi x 1.0^2) = 2.8 cm.

questions.explanation: Fulcrum at 45 cm: load is 30 cm from it, effort 45 cm from it; F x 45 = 30 x 30, F = 20 N.

questions.stem: A force of 100 N is used to kick a football of mass 0.8 kg. Find the velocity with which the ball moves if it takes 0.8 s to be kicked.
questions.explanation: Impulse Ft = mv: v = 100 x 0.8 / 0.8 = 100 m/s.

Thermal equilibrium between two objects exists when
options: The heat capacities of both objects are the same
One object loses heat continuously to the other
The temperatures of both objects are equal
The quantity of heat in both objects is the same
questions.explanation: There is no net heat flow when the two objects are at the same temperature.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: If an object is placed between two parallel plane mirrors with their reflecting surfaces facing each other, how many images of the object will be formed?
questions.explanation: n = 360/theta - 1; for parallel mirrors theta = 0, so the number of images is infinite.

questions.stem: A 2 000 W electric heater is used to heat a metal object of mass 5 kg initially at 10°C. If a temperature rise of 30°C is obtained after 10 min, the heat capacity of the material is
questions.explanation: Heat capacity = Pt/rise = 2000 x 600 / 30 = 4.0 x 10^4 J/°C.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: By what factor will the size of an object placed 10 cm from a convex lens be increased if the image is seen on a screen placed 25 cm from the lens?
questions.explanation: Magnification = v/u = 25/10 = 2.5.

questions.stem: On a fairly cool rainy day when the temperature is 20°C, the length of a steel railroad track is 20 m. What will be its length on a hot dry day when the temperature is 40°C?
questions.explanation: With the linear expansivity of steel (about 1.1 x 10^-5 K^-1, not given in the question), delta L = 20 x 1.1 x 10^-5 x 20 = 0.004 m, so the length is 20.004 m.

questions.stem: If 1.2 x 10^6 J of heat energy is given off in 1 s from a vessel maintained at a temperature gradient of 30 K m^-1, the surface area of the vessel is [Thermal conductivity of the vessel = 400 W m^-1 K^-1]

T (°C): 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 40, 60

questions.explanation: RH = actual VP / SVP at that temperature = 10/17.50 x 100% = 57%.

questions.topic: Reflection of light at plane and curved surfaces
questions.stem: At what position will an object be placed in front of a concave mirror in order to obtain an image at infinity?
options: Between the principal focus and the centre of curvature
At the pole of the mirror
questions.explanation: Rays from an object at the principal focus are reflected parallel, so the image is at infinity.

questions.stem: An open pipe closed at one end produces its first fundamental note. If the velocity of sound in air is v and l the length of the pipe, the frequency of the note is
questions.explanation: For a pipe closed at one end, l = wavelength/4 at the fundamental, so f = v/4l.

questions.explanation: Wavelength = 1 m; the shortest resonating air column is wavelength/4 = 0.25 m, so the maximum water height is 1.2 - 0.25 = 0.95 m.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane and curved surfaces

options: Incident angle is equal to the angle of refraction
Incident angle is equal to the angle of emergence
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation the ray passes symmetrically through the prism, so the angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence.

questions.stem:

II. It is more easily magnetized than steel
III. It is more easily demagnetized than steel
IV. It produces a stronger magnet than steel
Which combination of the above makes iron preferable to steel in the making of electromagnets?
questions.explanation: Soft iron is used because it magnetizes and demagnetizes easily, so the magnet switches off with the current.

Exerted on a stationary charge at the point

Metals have forbidden gaps while semiconductors have not
While the resistance of metals decreases with temperature, the reverse is the case for semiconductors

questions.explanation: This is short sight (myopia), which is corrected with a diverging (concave) lens.

questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids such as metals.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: All four involve equal and opposite action-reaction forces: walking pushes back on the ground and the ground pushes the person forward.

questions.explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally: 40/0.4 = 400/A, so A = 4 m^2.

questions.explanation: The de Broglie relation λ = h/p links wavelength (a wave property) to momentum (a particle property).

options: They have electrons and holes at high temperatures
Their resistance is constantly changing with temperature
questions.explanation: A negative temperature coefficient means resistance falls as temperature rises.

questions.stem: Fluorescent tubes produce light by the
options: Refraction of light by gas molecules
Thermal agitation of electrons in the tube

Commutator should be replaced with slit rings

Armature coil should be made of silver

questions.stem: Transverse waves can be distinguished from longitudinal waves using the characteristic of
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarized.

questions.stem: When left in a freezer, a bottle full of water cracks on freezing into ice because of the
options: Decrease in the volume of water
Increase in the volume of water

questions.topic: Elasticity: Hooke's law and Young's modulus

questions.explanation: Shiny silvered surfaces are poor emitters of radiant heat.

questions.stem: The instrument used for securing a large number of similar charges by induction is called

X-rays are electromagnetic radiations while gamma rays are negatively charged radiations
X-rays have higher frequencies than gamma rays
X-rays are more penetrating than gamma rays

A person touching the appliances is safe from electric shock
The appliances are maintained at a higher p.d. than the earth
The appliances are maintained at a lower p.d. than the earth
